cna.title: Zammad: Incorrect Authorization and Improper Privilege Management

descriptions.value: Zammad is a web based open source helpdesk/customer support system. Prior to 7.0.2 and 7.1.0, this issue concerns a lack of discursive validation within the authorization cascade. It has been determined that the system-level enforcement of access restrictions during the initialization of new identity objects exhibits a discrepancy: Under specific conditions, the granular restrictions of the access key being used are overridden by the latent authorization authority of the parent account. Consequently, this means that the intended separation of functional areas is nullified, resulting in an uncontrolled expansion of administrative discretion. Due to this potential integrity breach of the entire trust environment, an immediate evaluation of the authorization hierarchies is imperative. Impact An attacker can create new administrator accounts despite token restrictions. This grants full access to all system data (tickets, customers, configuration) and allows the attacker to take complete control of the Zammad instance. Abuse Scenario The vulnerability stems from a lack of synergy between the token-based authorization logic and the target system's functional authorization hierarchy, which allows for iterative escalation of the privileged access context. This issue is fixed in versions 7.0.2 and 7.1.0.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server memory via DATA frames sent past the advertised receive window. The attacker requests a response larger than the 65,535-byte initial window and withholds WINDOW_UPDATE, so the stream process blocks while sending and stops reading, then floods small DATA frames on that stream. Every frame is queued in the stream's mailbox until the BEAM node runs out of memory.

Bandit.HTTP2.Connection.handle_frame/3 in lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex forwards each DATA frame to the stream process without consulting the receive window, and Bandit.HTTP2.FlowControl.compute_recv_window/2 replenishes the window as data arrives rather than as it is consumed, and never answers a violation with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.

This issue affects bandit: from 0.3.1 before 1.14.0.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* On an HTTP/2 connection, request a resource whose response exceeds 65,535 bytes and send no WINDOW_UPDATE. The server sends one window's worth and the stream blocks in send_data/3.
* Send 1-byte DATA frames on that stream in batches, ignoring the server's receive windows.
* Between batches, at intervals under 15 seconds, send a stream WINDOW_UPDATE with an increment of 1 to keep the blocked send alive.
* Send a PING. It is acknowledged, and the server has sent neither FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR nor GOAWAY while its memory grows with every frame.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Connection-level window (lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex, lib/bandit/http2/flow_control.ex)

The handle_frame/3 clause for DATA frames sends the payload to the stream process before any window is checked. It then calls compute_recv_window/2, which subtracts the frame size and, once the window drops below 2^30, advertises a WINDOW_UPDATE back up to 2^31-1. A negative window is accepted, so a peer that overruns the window is never refused, and the window refills when data arrives rather than when it is consumed.

2. Stream-level window (lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex)

The stream receive window is debited only when the stream process reads the DATA message, and it never rejects a violation either.

3. Accumulation

While send_data/3 waits for send window, its selective receive matches only window updates and resets, so DATA messages pile up unread in the mailbox. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE of 1 byte, sent at intervals under the 15-second send timeout, keeps the stream alive while the attacker floods 1-byte DATA frames.

descriptions.value:
Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server CPU via small SETTINGS or connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE frames. The attacker opens thousands of streams whose responses block on the connection send window, then sends cheap frames that each make the server walk the whole queue of blocked sends. In the reporter's run, with 3,000 blocked streams a single 9-byte SETTINGS frame took 133 ms to process.

do_pending_sends/2 in lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex retries every queued send and, before each retry, removes that entry from the queue with List.delete/2, so one frame costs O(n²) list operations for n blocked streams. max_concurrent_streams defaults to :infinity, so the attacker chooses n.

This issue affects bandit: from 0.3.4 before 1.14.0.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* On one HTTP/2 connection, send 3,000 requests to an endpoint with a 20 KB response body, and send no connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE, so the responses queue in pending_sends.
* Send an empty SETTINGS frame followed by a PING.
* Time the PING acknowledgement. In the reporter's run, the single 9-byte SETTINGS frame delayed it by 133 ms. Repeating the frame keeps the connection process busy.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Blocked sends

A response that outruns the connection send window is queued in pending_sends. With max_concurrent_streams defaulting to :infinity and no connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE from the client, every one of n streams ends up queued.

2. Trigger (lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex)

Every non-ACK SETTINGS frame and every WINDOW_UPDATE on stream 0 calls do_pending_sends/2. SETTINGS handling also sends deliver_send_window_update to every stream even when the window delta is 0, so unread messages pile up in the mailboxes of blocked streams.

3. Quadratic drain

do_pending_sends/2 walks the queue and calls List.delete/2 on the whole list before retrying each entry, putting it back at the front if the send is still blocked. One frame therefore costs O(n²) list operations, about 10^8 at n = 10,000.

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by escaping enum symbol values before rendering them.

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema field documentation allows code injection in generated Pydantic descriptions

descriptions.description: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.65.9 through 0.70.5, PydanticFieldRepresentation.add_field_properties inserts a schema field's doc value between the quotes of a generated pydantic.Field description argument without escaping it. A crafted quote can terminate the string and inject an expression evaluated during generated class definition, allowing arbitrary Python code execution for Pydantic and AvroDantic model generation. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by escaping the documentation value before rendering it.

cna.title: enclave-os-mini: RA-TLS challenge certificates were not bound to the TLS session

descriptions.value: Enclave OS Mini is a Rust-based runtime for confidential applications inside Intel SGX enclaves. Prior to wasm-v0.40.0, the SGX runtime's RA-TLS challenge certificate path placed the certificate public-key hash and client nonce in quote ReportData but omitted a value bound to the active TLS session. An attacker who obtained an enclave TLS private key could relay a genuine quote onto another connection, causing a relying party to accept an attacker-terminated connection as the attested enclave. This issue is fixed in wasm-v0.40.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cna.title: Wizarr: Authenticated Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in wizard step rendering leads to Remote Code Execution (RCE)

descriptions.value: Wizarr is an advanced user invitation and management system for Jellyfin, Plex, Emby, and other media servers. Prior to 2026.9.1, wizard step Markdown supplied through the editor or imported bundles was evaluated by app/blueprints/wizard/routes.py in the application's non-sandboxed Jinja2 environment with application globals exposed. An authenticated user able to create steps, or an administrator importing an untrusted bundle through POST /settings/wizard/import, could execute arbitrary Python when GET /wizard/{server}/{idx} rendered the stored step; app/jinja_filters.py and app/services/wizard_widgets.py contained additional evaluation sinks. This could execute operating-system commands as the application user, disclose the Flask SECRET_KEY, access connected service credentials and the database, and produce stored cross-site scripting. This issue is fixed in 2026.9.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

references.name: VDB-416189 | Studio-Saelix Sencho git-sources Browse API Endpoint outboundTarget.ts server-side request forgery

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was determined in Studio-Saelix Sencho up to 0.94.1. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file outboundTarget.ts of the component git-sources Browse API Endpoint. Executing a manipulation of the argument repo_url can lead to server-side request forgery. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The presence of this vulnerability remains uncertain at this time. This patch is called 79b86ddcd4aefdd6941f098e35990ab397b13c72. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue. The vendor explains: "Git repository access is an intentional, privileged administrative function. Sencho explicitly supports repositories hosted on private LAN, VPC, VPN, CGNAT, and IPv6 ULA networks. The report does not demonstrate a privilege-boundary bypass or access by an unprivileged user. We therefore dispute the CVE characterization of this behavior. As defense in depth, we have nevertheless hardened repository access. Git HTTPS and SSH connections now validate and pin DNS resolution, reject loopback, link-local, multicast, selected special-use and metadata targets, disable redirects and inherited proxy routing, and retain strict SSH host-key verification."

cna.title: DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl crash via type confusion in dbi_profile when a database handle is destroyed under a Profile Path with an {attr} element

solutions.value: Upgrade to DBI 1.656 or later.

descriptions.value:
DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl crash via type confusion in dbi_profile when a database handle is destroyed under a Profile Path with an {attr} element.

An {attr} element names a database handle attribute, which dbi_profile reads from the handle's inner hash. It expects the inner handle as a reference and dereferences it, but a handle that is being destroyed hands back the inner hash itself, so the dereference yields the hash's bucket array. A type check on that pointer usually fails and the call goes unprofiled. When the memory it addresses passes the check, the attribute lookup dereferences a NULL or invalid pointer and the process dies on SIGSEGV.

The Path is set by the application, by the Profile handle attribute, or by the DBI_PROFILE environment variable, so `DBI_PROFILE={ImplementorClass}` can crash an unmodified program.

descriptions.description: CWE-843 Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

descriptions.description: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema fixed namespaces allow code injection in generated annotations

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.38.0 through 0.70.5, BaseGenerator.parse_fixed inserts a fixed type's namespace value between quotes inside a generated types.confixed annotation without escaping or validating it. A crafted quote can terminate the namespace string and alter the surrounding annotation expression, which Python evaluates when the generated class is defined, allowing arbitrary code execution. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by requiring the namespace to be a dot-separated sequence of valid Avro names.

descriptions.description: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

Blinko through 1.8.8 allows directory traversal, overwriting startup files as root, via installPlugin. It builds the plugin install path from an unsanitized name in server/routerTrpc/plugin.ts, and the plugin.installPlugin tRPC procedure is open to any authenticated user. Because the official Docker image runs as root, an authenticated attacker overwrites a root-owned startup file and achieves remote code execution as root. Self-registration for an account may be possible.

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema allows code injection through record names in generated default factories

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: GLPI through 12.0.0 Missing Authorization via ajax/map.php

descriptions.value: GLPI through 12.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ajax/map.php that allows authenticated low-privileged users to search itemtypes they cannot view by omitting the canView() check. Attackers can submit crafted itemtype and search criteria for types like Contact, Supplier, Contract and Budget to obtain match counts, titles and coordinates within their entities.

cna.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Alosuite that affects the delivery note functionality.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-592 Stored XSS

solutions.value: The manufacturer has indicated that the vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 26_04_15.03_10 of ALO Suite, released in April 2026. It is recommended that you use the patched version.

supportingMedia.value: The manufacturer has indicated that the vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 26_04_15.03_10 of ALO Suite, released in April 2026. It is recommended that you use the patched version.

descriptions.value:
A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Alosuite that affects the delivery note functionality. Insufficient sanitization and encoding of the specified fields allow JavaScript to be stored, which executes in other users’ browsers when they view the affected records. Exploitation requires authenticated access to the affected functionality. The code can alter the displayed content and perform actions within the context of the victim’s session. The list of features, parameters, and endpoints is as follows:

CVE-2026-108053: Nombre in ‘/CuentasCorrientes/Create’;

cna.title: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 Missing Authorization via /airag/extData/deleteBatch

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 Missing Authorization via /airag/extData/deleteBatch

descriptions.value: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AiragExtDataController deleteBatch handler that allows any authenticated user to delete AI evaluator records. Low-privileged attackers can send comma-separated ids to DELETE /airag/extData/deleteBatch, which lacks owner or tenant checks, deleting other users' evaluator and test-tracking records.

cna.title: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 Missing Authorization via /sys/api/queryUserRoles

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 Missing Authorization via /sys/api/queryUserRoles

descriptions.value: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the queryUserRoles handler of SystemApiController that lets authenticated users read any user's role codes. Low-privileged attackers can send GET requests to /sys/api/queryUserRoles with an arbitrary username to enumerate role assignments and identify administrator accounts.

cna.title: zotero-mcp 0.10.0 through 0.14.1 SSRF via zotero_add_by_url Tool

credits.value: HaiND from the Post and Telecommunication Institute of Technology

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: zotero-mcp 0.10.0 through 0.14.1 SSRF via zotero_add_by_url Tool

descriptions.value: zotero-mcp 0.10.0 through 0.14.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to reach internal services because _fetch_embedded_metadata fetches URLs without destination validation. Attackers can steer the agent via prompt injection into calling zotero_add_by_url, causing requests to loopback, private, or link-local hosts directly or via redirects, leaking citation meta-tags and error details.

cna.title: WP Booking System <= 2.1.0.3 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Disclosure via 'wpbs_action=email_logs' Action

descriptions.value: The WP Booking System – Booking Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0.3 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the stored notification email body of any booking by iterating booking_id and email_log_id, exposing customer PII including names, email addresses, phone numbers, messages, and booking dates intended to be visible only to administrators. This is exploitable by any Subscriber-level user because admin_init fires on profile.php, a wp-admin page accessible to all authenticated users.

cna.title: Speedtest Tracker through 1.15.0 IP Allowlist Bypass via X-Forwarded-For Spoofing

credits.value: HaiND from the Post and Telecommunication Institute of Technology

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Speedtest Tracker through 1.15.0 IP Allowlist Bypass via X-Forwarded-For Spoofing

descriptions.value: Speedtest Tracker through 1.15.0 contains an IP allowlist bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to evade ALLOWED_IPS and Prometheus allowlists by spoofing X-Forwarded-For headers. descriptions.value: JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to delete other users' AI voice records by supplying an arbitrary userId to DELETE /airag/voice/deleteVoiceRecord. descriptions.value: Wanwu before 0.6.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows any authenticated enabled user to delete other users' legacy AppKeys by supplying a numeric apiId. Attackers can iterate sequential key IDs against DELETE /v1/appspace/app/key to revoke AppKeys across organizations, breaking MCP and OpenAPI clients until owners issue new keys.

cna.title: Password Reset Code Accessible in User Listing API

descriptions.value: CAPEC-50 Password Recovery Exploitation

solutions.value: Disable the password reset feature in the web interface. This vulnerability is addressed in Remote Ops Agent version 2.1.

supportingMedia.value: Disable the password reset feature in the web interface. This vulnerability is addressed in Remote Ops Agent version 2.1.

descriptions.value:
An administrator could retrieve the password reset code for any user and take over the account.



The password reset codes were included in the output of an API and could be used to reset the password of any account. The API is limited to use by administrator accounts only.



An attacker who already has administrative access to the application could compromise the credentials of other accounts on the application. Device credentials and customer data cannot be accessed with this vulnerability.

cna.title: Shiny for Python - Path traversal in bookmark restore

descriptions.value: Shiny for Python is a framework for building interactive web applications in Python. From 1.4.0 until 1.6.4, bookmark restore accepts a client-supplied state_id and joins it into the server-side shiny_bookmarks directory without validating that it is a single safe path segment. An unauthenticated request can use parent-directory segments or an absolute path to make the server open input.json and values.json outside the bookmark store, even when bookmark_store is set to disable. In applications configured with bookmark_store set to server and using ui.input_file(), the restore handler can additionally copy and expose an attacker-selected file from an attacker-selected directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

cna.title: Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker: Repeated rejected temporary destination consumer requests can lead to broker OOM

descriptions.value:
Denial of Service via OOM vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker.



An authenticated OpenWire client that sends a ConsumerInfo for a temporary queue/topic owned by another connection is rejected with InvalidDestinationException, but the rejected Subscription is left behind in the region's subscriptions map. Repeating the request leaks broker heap until OOM because the broker does not clean up the rejected subscriptions in the map.



This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; ActiveMQ Broker: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3, or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: Apache CXF: Prevent unbounded XML document size in StaxUtils by adding default element and character limits

descriptions.value:
By default, StaxUtils placed no limit on the total number of elements or the total number of characters in an XML document. A very large request could therefore use a lot of memory and CPU during parsing, especially where CXF builds a DOM from the input (for example SAAJ or WS-Security), and could cause a denial of service when no request size limit was configured. Both limits now have defaults: the maximum element count is 100 × maxChildElements (5,000,000 by default), and the maximum document size is 256M characters. Applications that process larger documents can raise the limits with the org.apache.cxf.stax.maxElementCount and org.apache.cxf.stax.maxXMLCharacters properties.
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

cna.title: Mutter: mutter: client-triggered use-after-free in wayland color-management icc image description path

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Calif.io (security-disclosures@calif.io), in collaboration with Anthropic for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Do not run untrusted applications in the affected Wayland session. Limit Wayland socket access for untrusted clients.

descriptions.value: A use-after-free flaw was found in mutter in the Wayland color-management ICC image-description path. A local attacker who can run a malicious Wayland client can destroy a wp_image_description_v1 resource while an asynchronous ICC file read is still in progress. When the read completes, the compositor uses the freed wl_resource, writes into freed memory, and frees a pointer derived from that memory. This can crash the GNOME session and may allow arbitrary code execution within the compositor process.
A vulnerability allowing an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authorization on the CDP Coordinator Service.

cna.title: temporal-proxy payload decryption is not bound to the request namespace

credits.value: Reported internally at Temporal Technologies, Inc.
Praetorian, who independently reported this issue responsibly to Temporal Technologies

descriptions.value: Disclosure, across the namespace authorization boundary, of payloads the proxy encrypted: Workflow and Activity inputs and results, and Signal and Update arguments. Encrypted payloads cannot be modified through this issue, and data the proxy does not encrypt is not affected. No availability impact was identified.

solutions.value: Upgrade to temporal-proxy 0.9.0 or later and set encryption.namespaceBinding to strict. Fixed releases record the namespace in each payload they encrypt and, in strict mode, refuse to decrypt a payload recorded for another namespace or for none, including through the codec server's /decode endpoint, which then requires the caller to name a namespace. The setting has no default and must be set whenever encryption keys are configured. The off and permissive modes exist to migrate payloads encrypted by earlier releases, which carry no namespace, and do not close this issue; move to strict once the vault_unbound_opens_total and vault_namespace_mismatches_total metrics have stayed at zero for longer than namespace retention. Payloads carried in Nexus operations are not compared, because they cross namespaces by design.

The setting has no default and must be set whenever encryption keys are configured. The off and permissive modes exist to migrate payloads encrypted by earlier releases, which carry no namespace, and do not close this issue; move to strict once the vault_unbound_opens_total and vault_namespace_mismatches_total metrics have stayed at zero for longer than namespace retention. Payloads carried in Nexus operations are not compared, because they cross namespaces by design.

references.name: Vault.Open in temporal-proxy 0.8.0, which takes no namespace
KEKRegistry.Decrypt in temporal-proxy 0.8.0, which selects the KEK by the identifier in the payload
AES-256-GCM sealed and opened with no associated data in temporal-proxy 0.8.0
Design discussion of associated data in the payload encryption scheme

workarounds.value: Until a fixed release is deployed, serve namespaces that must stay isolated from each other through separate proxy deployments, or use KMS key policies that let each proxy use only the keys of the namespaces it serves. Giving each namespace its own key on a single proxy does not help, because that proxy holds all of them. Leaving the codec server disabled closes the /decode route only.

Giving each namespace its own key on a single proxy does not help, because that proxy holds all of them. Leaving the codec server disabled closes the /decode route only.

descriptions.value: temporal-proxy 0.2.0 through 0.8.0 does not bind encrypted payloads to the namespace they were encrypted for. When payload encryption is enabled, the proxy chooses the decryption key by an identifier stored in the payload rather than by the namespace of the request, and nothing in the ciphertext records that namespace. A caller whom the proxy authorizes only for namespace B, and who has obtained an encrypted payload from namespace A, can therefore have the proxy decrypt it. In 0.8.0, the caller can submit the payload to the codec server's /decode endpoint. In every affected version, a caller who can also write to namespace B on the Temporal server directly can place the payload there and read it back through the proxy. This holds whether namespaces share the default key or each has its own, because a single proxy holds every key it is configured with. The issue does not give the attacker encrypted payloads they could not already obtain, and does not allow encrypted payloads to be modified.

descriptions.description: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

configurations.value: Exploitation requires all of the following. Payload encryption is enabled; it is off by default. Callers are restricted to particular namespaces, either by an authorization extension (0.5.0 and later) or by per-namespace authorization on the upstream Temporal server. The attacker is authorized for one namespace and holds an encrypted payload from another, obtained outside the proxy, for example through read access on the Temporal server, an export, or the persistence store. Either the codec server is enabled (0.8.0 only, off by default), or the attacker can write to their own namespace on the Temporal server directly. In affected versions, the built-in static-token and JWKS authenticators do not restrict callers by namespace, so a deployment that relies on them alone already lets every caller read every namespace through the proxy, and this issue crosses no further boundary there.

cna.title: Privasys Intra-handshake attested TLS implementation is vulnerable to TOCTOU Attacks

descriptions.value: Privasys Remote Attestation TLS Clients provides multi-language utilities for verifying attested TLS connections. Before 0.9.1, an attacker with local access could modify workload code, data, and configuration at any time after successful connection establishment. Once Evidence was successfully appraised and the connection was established, there was a window of vulnerability from the establishment of the connection to the termination of the connection where an attacker could modify the state of the workload and platform at runtime on the TLS endpoint acting as the Attester. This vulnerability was possible because Privasys/ra-tls-clients performed attestation only once in the lifetime of the connection (at connection establishment time), and the verifying peer continued to believe that the state was the same as in the initial Evidence throughout, whereas it could be stale at some point in time. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.9.1.

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema record documentation can terminate generated class docstrings

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.40.0 through 0.70.5, ClassRepresentation.render_docstring copies a schema record's doc value into a generated triple-double-quoted class docstring without escaping quotes or backslashes. A crafted triple-quote sequence can close the docstring and inject statements into the generated class body, while a trailing backslash can escape the generated closing delimiter, allowing Python code execution during module import. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by escaping quotes, backslashes, and unsafe control characters before rendering docstrings.

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.44.0 through 0.70.5, the Pydantic and AvroDantic model generators insert a schema field's pydantic-class value after pydantic. in a generated field annotation without safely restricting the expression. Because annotations are evaluated when the generated module is imported, a crafted value can execute arbitrary Python code. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by restricting the value to a bare name or a call to a bare name with literal arguments.

solutions.value: No fixed release as of 2026-10-11. A community fix exists as VeraCrypt pull request #1866 (commit 000bcf4): on dismount, explicitly shut down the auxiliary FUSE-T service through an authenticated control endpoint and wait for it to terminate before reporting the dismount as complete. The maintainer described the same approach in issue #1779. The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is unaffected.

supportingMedia.value: No fixed release as of 2026-10-11. references.name: Original public report (June 2026) with maintainer acknowledgment and diagnosis
Independent report with first process-level diagnosis and maintainer reply (June 2026)
Consolidated issue: reproductions, lsof evidence, kernel panic analysis, status
Community fix: terminate auxiliary FUSE-T service on dismount

workarounds.value: Use the macFUSE build of VeraCrypt instead of the FUSE-T build (the maintainer's recommended interim mitigation; the macFUSE build is not affected). If staying on the FUSE-T build: After dismounting your volumes, restart macOS to end any surviving sessions. Using the affected FUSE-T build again can recreate the problem. Updating FUSE-T alone hasn't been verified as a fix. A process name match can't reliably identify every surviving VeraCrypt service. Manual process killing shouldn't be treated as proof that access has ended, and killing a service while a volume is still mounted can interrupt writes.

descriptions.value: VeraCrypt 1.26.29 (FUSE-T build) on macOS sometimes allows unintended access to decrypted data. It does not terminate the FUSE-T auxiliary service (go-nfsv4) and its associated VeraCrypt core-service helper processes when a volume is dismounted. After VeraCrypt reports the volume as dismounted, the auxiliary mount continues to serve the decrypted volume image (volume.dmg) over a loopback SMB session, and the leaked processes retain an open handle to the underlying raw device. A local user or process can therefore remount and access the decrypted volume without the passphrase, e.g., by reopening a previously accessed path (such as through a macOS Open Recent menu) or by attaching volume.dmg from the stale auxiliary mount. (The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is not affected.)

cna.title: HestiaCP Low-Privileged User to Root via Config-Field Injection and PATH Hijacking

descriptions.value: Hestia Control Panel is a lightweight and powerful control panel for the modern web. From version 1.9.7 through 1.10.4, update_object_value() in func/main.sh does not escape single quotes when writing a custom document-root value to a user's web.conf file, allowing a low-privileged authenticated panel user with a web domain to inject an additional PATH field. When the user invokes the ordinary Search feature, the root-privileged v-search-user-object script loads the forged field through parse_object_kv_list_non_eval(), which permits reserved shell-variable names and globally replaces PATH before invoking column without an absolute path. By placing a malicious column executable in the injected search path, the user can execute arbitrary code as root. This residual vulnerability was introduced when version 1.9.7 replaced the raw eval sink addressed by CVE-2026-84984 with parse_object_kv_list_non_eval(), and it is fixed in version 1.10.5.

workarounds.value: Restrict write access to the cache directories and all of their parent directories to the nginx user only, and do not run nginx and untrusted application code (for example PHP-FPM) as the same user. Remove any symbolic links found inside configured cache paths (find <cache_path> -type l). These measures also limit the similar traversal in nginx's own cache loader, which the fix in the module does not change.

descriptions.value: ngx_cache_purge before 3.0.4 can allow file deletion via a symlink attack in certain situations where nginx and a served application (e.g., WordPress) run under the same user account. The attacker must be able to create a symlink inside the cache path. Version 3.0.4 fixes this for the case of a symlink created at an arbitrary earlier time, but does not resolve an applicable TOCTOU race condition. (The ngx_cache_purge module follows symlinks while walking the cache directory tree during purge operations. The module relies on nginx's ngx_walk_tree(), which relies on stat() and therefore follows symlinks.)

configurations.value: nginx built with the ngx_cache_purge module and a proxy, fastcgi, scgi or uwsgi cache path with purge walks in use (purge_all, a wildcard purge, or cache_purge_vary_aware; arbitrary file deletion requires purge_all or a wildcard purge whose key reduces to an empty prefix), and an attacker able to create a symbolic link inside the cache path, for example when nginx and a web application run as the same user. The attacker does not need PURGE access: any legitimate purge of this kind, such as an automatic purge_all issued by a cache plugin, triggers the traversal.

descriptions.description: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

descriptions.value: radare2 is a UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. Prior to 6.2.2, attacker-controlled data from several binary format plugins could reach RBinInfo->bclass. Opening or analyzing a crafted Pebble or Sega Mega Drive binary could place a dbg:// URI in bclass, causing radare2 to reopen the input through the debug input/output plugin and ultimately pass attacker-controlled arguments to execvp(). cna.title: Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker: The broker does not verify user provided connection id matches connection

descriptions.value:
Improper input validation vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB.



The ActiveMQ broker resolves connection, session and consumer state from ids that are user provided and in some scenarios does not validate that they ids are bound to that user. This allows an authenticated client to spoof another user's ids. This allows:





  *   an authenticated client consumes from another connection's temporary queue/topic by putting the victim's connection id in its own ConsumerId, bypassing the broker-side ownership check. 
  *  a duplicate ConsumerId registration is only logged, after which the attacker's RemoveInfo or disconnect tears down the victim's live subscription
  *  a forged MessageAck for the victim's ConsumerId permanently deletes an in-flight, unacknowledged message.








This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3, or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, Worksheet\Drawing::setPath validates only the initial external-image URL with setIsWhitelisted when setAllowExternalImages is enabled. The HTTP stream context permits PHP to follow a redirect without applying the callback to the redirected URL, so a permitted image host can redirect the server to an internal address and cause a blind GET request. The response body is not returned to the attacker because the reader validates the downloaded content as an image and removes the temporary file, but internal GET-driven endpoints, network reachability, and cloud metadata endpoints may be reached. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

cna.title: Privasys rustls fork: RA-TLS challenge mode did not bind attestation evidence to the TLS session

descriptions.value: Privasys rustls is a maintained fork of the rustls TLS library that adds RA-TLS challenge and channel-binding support. Prior to privasys-v0.8.1, the fork emitted RA-TLS challenge certificates whose quote ReportData was bound to the certificate public key and client nonce but not to the active TLS session. An attacker who obtained an enclave TLS private key could relay a genuine quote onto another connection, causing a relying party to accept an attacker-terminated connection as the attested enclave. This issue is fixed in privasys-v0.8.1.

descriptions.value: DDEV is an open-source tool for running local web development environments for PHP and Node.js. From 1.25.2 until 1.25.4, Untar in pkg/archive/archive.go validates an absolute tar symlink target after rebasing it beneath dest, but creates the symlink with the raw absolute Linkname. cna.title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header

descriptions.value:
Symfony is a PHP framework for web and console applications and a set of reusable PHP components. Prior to versions 5.4.54, 6.4.46, 7.4.19, and 8.1.7, HeaderUtils::split() parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a (?<!\s) lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. HeaderBag calls it for the Cache-Control header whenever a Request is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.



A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, preg_match_all() gives up at pcre.backtrack_limit and split() returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.



This issue affects symfony/http-foundation v4.1.0-BETA1 through v5.4.53, v6.0.0-BETA1 through v6.4.45, v7.0.0-BETA1 through v7.4.18, and v8.0.0-BETA1 through v8.1.6.

descriptions.value: The 10Web Booster – Website speed optimization, Cache & Page Speed optimizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.34.10 via the compressCustom function. This is due to missing file type validation and extension filtering on the page_id parameter, combined with a world-readable leaked nonce that bypasses authentication checks. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. This exploit chain requires obtaining the plugin's REST nonce (tenwebio_rest), which is automatically serialized to a world-readable file under wp-content/uploads/ whenever a bulk optimisation batch pauses; because the nonce is generated in a cron/loopback context with a user ID of 0, it is valid for unauthenticated visitors.

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema allows code injection through fixed-type aliases supplied as a bare string

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.38.0 through 0.70.5, BaseGenerator.parse_fixed interpolates a fixed type's aliases value directly into a generated types.confixed annotation. cna.title: LoopX serve-status permissive CORS policy exposes control-plane state and private Markdown files

descriptions.value: Open and provider-neutral, LoopX is a lightweight state kernel and local-first control plane for loop engineering. From version 0.0.1 until 0.4.5, `loopx serve-status` in `loopx/status_server.py` uses `StatusRequestHandler._send_json()` and `do_OPTIONS()` to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` for unauthenticated responses on predictable loopback ports. A remote attacker can cause an operator who visits attacker-controlled web content to issue cross-origin requests to `GET /status.json`, `GET /review-material?goal_id=...&path=...`, `GET /`, and `POST /control-plane/configure-goal/dry-run`, exposing control-plane state, goal and run information, local absolute paths, private Markdown files below registered goal roots, and dry-run configuration projections. The affected routes do not provide cross-origin writes or arbitrary-file access. This issue is fixed in version 0.4.5.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via Double-Encoded unentity() TOCTOU Allows XXE and Denial of Service

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. From 3.3.0 until 3.10.8 and 5.10.0, Reader\Xml passes stored SpreadsheetML XML through XmlScanner::scan in Xml::canRead and Xml::trySimpleXMLLoadStringPrivate, while Xml::unentity decodes numeric entities only after each DOCTYPE pattern check. A double-encoded less-than character is reduced by the first callback to another encoded character and by the second callback to a literal less-than sign, so SimpleXML receives an unchecked DOCTYPE and entity declaration. Processing attacker-controlled SpreadsheetML XML can cause entity-expansion denial of service and can permit local file access or SSRF on PHP before 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is enabled. This issue is fixed in versions 3.10.8 and 5.10.0.

cna.title: TinaCMS admin preview iframe loads an attacker-controlled origin from the URL fragment

descriptions.value: Tina is a headless content management system. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted link to a signed-in editor, cause the admin to frame an attacker origin, and have that frame treated as the trusted preview. The attacker-controlled frame can submit GraphQL reads or mutations that the admin executes with the editor credentials, exposing or modifying protected content. cna.title: Improper Authentication and Credential Exposure in Multiple TP-Link Kasa Devices

credits.value: M. Hammad Mazhar from University of Northern Colorado & Madeline Cooreman

descriptions.value: CAPEC-115 Authentication Bypass

Multiple
Kasa devices contain an improper authentication vulnerability in the local
device-management protocol. An unauthenticated adjacent attacker may send
management instructions to an affected device without adequate authentication
or authorization, allowing modification of the device state or management
settings. Under certain usage conditions involving interaction between the
user, mobile application, and device-cloud service, insufficient protection of
account-related communications may also expose account information.









Successful
exploitation may allow an unauthenticated adjacent-network attacker to perform
unauthorized device-management actions and disrupt legitimate user control.
Under certain conditions, account-related information may also be exposed,
potentially leading to compromise of the associated cloud account.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via ISO-2022 Escape Sequences Allows XXE and Denial of Service

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, XmlScanner::scan in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php uses a DOCTYPE detection pattern that accounts for NUL-byte interleaving but not ISO-2022 escape sequences in XLSX XML parts. The escape sequences prevent the scanner from matching the declaration, and XML charset normalization then removes the escape bytes before parsing, exposing a valid DOCTYPE and entity definitions. Processing an attacker-controlled XLSX can therefore cause entity-expansion denial of service on supported PHP versions and can permit local file access or SSRF on PHP before 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is enabled. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

cna.title: Busybox: busybox: tar extraction-root escape via deferred symlink/hardlink creation bypasses cve-2026-26158 fix

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank TAE3 for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Avoid extracting tar archives from untrusted sources using busybox, especially with elevated privileges or into a directory that will be reused for a subsequent extraction. If untrusted archives must be processed, extract into a freshly created, isolated directory with minimal privileges on a single filesystem boundary and discard it (including any links left on disk) after each extraction.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in busybox. The tar applet's deferred link-creation handling for symlink and hardlink entries with unsafe-looking targets does not validate that the resolved destination remains inside the extraction directory once the deferred link is created. An attacker can craft a tar archive using a symlink target of exactly '..' combined with a deferred hardlink to create a new file outside the extraction directory, or reuse an extraction directory across two archives to replace an existing file outside it. If the archive is extracted with elevated privileges, this flaw can lead to privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

cna.title: Model Context Protocol Java SDK HTTP server transports allow memory exhaustion through unbounded request bodies

descriptions.value: The Model Context Protocol Java SDK is the official Java SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From version 0.8.0 through 0.12.0 in the io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp artifact, from 0.13.0 through 0.18.3 and 1.0.0 through 1.1.3 in io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp-core, and from mcp-core 2.0.0-M1 through 2.0.0, the Servlet-based SSE, Streamable HTTP, and Stateless server transports read an HTTP request body into memory without enforcing a maximum size. An unauthenticated remote client able to reach an affected transport can stream an arbitrarily large POST body, including with chunked transfer encoding, until the Java process exhausts its heap and becomes unavailable. Authentication, Origin or Host validation, or an upstream request-size limit can reject the request before the vulnerable read. cna.title: ExtUtils::Typemaps::STL::String versions before 1.06 for Perl T_STD_STRING typemap may read the SV length before stringifying the argument

timeline.value: Issue reported in bugtracker for ExtUtils::Typemaps::Default version 1.05.
Fix committed to the repository. Bugtracker issue closed.
ExtUtils::Typemaps::Default version 1.06 released with a fix.

solutions.value:
Upgrade to ExtUtils::Typemaps::Default version 1.06 or later.

Rebuild any modules that use ExtUtils::Typemaps::Default as part of their build process.

workarounds.value: For deployments that cannot be upgraded, ensure that arguments passed to modules that use ExtUtils::Typemaps::Default are strngified.

descriptions.value:
ExtUtils::Typemaps::STL::String versions before 1.06 for Perl T_STD_STRING typemap may read the SV length before stringifying the argument.

The typemap uses

    $var = std::string( SvPV_nolen($arg), SvCUR($arg) )

However, evaluation order for C++ arguments is not specified, and some compilers may produce code that evalutes SvCUR($arg) first.

When $arg is not a string (for example, an interger, number or a reference) then SvCUR will return an invalid value, and the program may abort or segfault.

cna.title: @fastify/jwt vulnerable to missing token expiration when temporal options cannot be parsed

descriptions.value: @fastify/jwt is a JSON Web Token plugin for the Fastify web framework. In versions before 10.2.3, a time span passed to expiresIn, notBefore, or maxAge that the plugin's parser cannot read, such as a compound span, a month unit, an ISO 8601 duration, a decimal comma, or a value with surrounding whitespace, is silently dropped instead of refused. On the signing path this produces a token with no expiration claim that never expires, and on the verification path a configured maxAge stops being enforced, so a token that should be rejected for age is accepted. The issue is fixed in @fastify/jwt 10.2.3, and users should upgrade to 10.2.3 or later. As a workaround, pass these options as a number of seconds, or verify that any time-span string parses to a finite value before relying on it.

solutions.value: Upgrade to traverse 0.6.12 or later, or, on older release lines, to 0.5.3, 0.4.7, or 0.3.10.

workarounds.value: Do not pass untrusted paths to set(). If that is not possible, require every path segment to be a string other than __proto__, constructor, or prototype, and confirm that each intermediate value along the path is an object before calling set().

supportingMedia.value: Do not pass untrusted paths to set(). If that is not possible, require every path segment to be a string other than __proto__, constructor, or prototype, and confirm that each intermediate value along the path is an object before calling set().

descriptions.value: traverse (npm) versions 0.3.6 through 0.3.9, 0.4.0 through 0.4.6, 0.5.0 through 0.5.2, and 0.6.0 through 0.6.11 allow prototype pollution through set(). When the path passed to set() crosses a primitive value, the next path segment is resolved on that primitive's built-in prototype, so an application that passes an untrusted path to set() lets an attacker add or overwrite properties of String.prototype, Number.prototype, or Boolean.prototype using plain JSON data, for example traverse({ name: 'bob' }).set(['name', '__proto__', 'polluted'], 'yes'). Object.prototype was reachable only with a non-data path segment, such as an object whose toString returns a different value on each call, or through a Proxy that accepts an assignment without storing it. This is fixed in 0.3.10, 0.4.7, 0.5.3, and 0.6.12.

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which unfolds a header value in one pass and searches a header being read only in what each read adds. Until then: lower the maximum message size, which bounds the cost (it grows with the square of the value's size); remove such a message over POP3; or keep the REST listener off (RestApiPort 0, the default).

descriptions.value: Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the decoding of message header fields in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the IMAP, SMTP and POP3 services, or the webmail, unavailable by sending a message. The server unfolded a decoded header value by finding each line break from the end of the value and removing it, moving the rest of the value each time, so its work grew with the square of the number of line breaks, and an RFC 2047 encoded word may decode to any number of them. A received message whose Subject or other header field holds such a value keeps a worker thread busy for minutes or longer each time the value is read: when the recipient's IMAP client searches, sorts or threads the folder by a header, when the webmail lists the folder, and, where configured, when a rule tests a header, a spam tag is added to the Subject or an abuse report is read during delivery. The IMAP worker threads are shared with SMTP and POP3, so a few such messages stop those services responding. The server's reading of a message header from its file also searched everything read so far after each 4,000 bytes, costing seconds for a header of tens of megabytes.

descriptions.value: The AsyncHttpClient (AHC) library allows Java applications to easily execute HTTP requests and asynchronously process HTTP responses. AuthenticatorUtils.computeExpectedRspAuth returns no expected value for auth-int, and Interceptors treats that result as unverifiable but nonfatal, so a response with an invalid rspauth value is accepted. descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.3.1 to 2.11.0, agile decryption accepts an attacker-controlled spinCount and performs that many password-key derivation iterations before verifier validation. OpenFile reaches agileDecrypt, which passes the unbounded spinCount to convertPasswdToKey before password verification. When a crafted OLE encrypted-workbook header supplies an excessive spinCount and the file is opened, the key-derivation loop performs unbounded attacker-selected work and cannot be cancelled, allowing an attacker to consume a CPU core for an attacker-controlled duration. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: Excelize ANCHORARRAY: mutually-referencing array formulas recurse unboundedly via re-entrant CalcCellValue, causing a fatal stack overflow

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.8.1 to 2.11.0, ANCHORARRAY recursively calls the exported CalcCellValue function, creating a fresh calculation context at each cycle and bypassing in-flight and iteration controls. ANCHORARRAY calls CalcCellValue instead of cellResolver, so each recursive hop receives a new calcContext and loses cycle state. When mutually referencing dynamic-array formulas are evaluated directly or through formula-evaluating APIs, each recursion hop resets the cycle budget and prevents completion-based caches from breaking the cycle, allowing an attacker to cause a fatal Go stack overflow and abort the process. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: @fastify/reply-from vulnerable to improper certificate validation in built-in HTTPS transports

descriptions.value: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP or HTTPS server. In versions prior to 12.7.0, all of the built-in HTTPS transports override the secure default and set rejectUnauthorized to false, so the proxy does not verify the TLS certificate of the upstream even when the application points it at an https upstream in the default configuration. An on-path network attacker can therefore impersonate the configured HTTPS upstream, read the credentials and request bodies the proxy forwards, and return forged responses that the application trusts. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.7.0, and users should upgrade to 12.7.0 or later. As a workaround, pass an explicit rejectUnauthorized true on the transport, supply an already configured undici instance, or use the undici global agent.

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose string replacement and removal write their result in one pass. Until then: lower the maximum message size, which bounds the cost (it grows with the square of the HTML's size); remove such a message over IMAP or POP3; or keep the REST listener off (RestApiPort 0, the default).

descriptions.value: Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the REST API (6.3.3 through 6.3.5) and the IMAP PREVIEW response (6.2.22 through 6.3.5) of Progressive Robot hMailServer allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the webmail, the administration console and the REST API unavailable by sending a message. To show a snippet of each message in a folder's message list, the server decoded the character entity references of a message that has an HTML part and no text part with a string replacement whose work grew with the square of their number. A received HTML-only message holding a very large number of entity references therefore keeps one of the listener's four worker threads busy for minutes or longer each time the recipient's webmail lists the folder, without the message being opened, so that a few such listings leave the HTTP listener unable to answer anybody. The IMAP PREVIEW response read such text the same way, holding an IMAP thread for each client that asks for the preview of such a message. The flaw is in the server's shared string class, whose replace and remove both ran in quadratic time.

Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the WebSocket streaming client in agentjido req_llm allows an on-path attacker to read and modify OpenAI WebSocket sessions, including the authorization bearer token, via a TLS certificate the client does not trust. x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Entry points. ReqLLM.Providers.OpenAI.WebSocket.responses_url/2 and realtime_url/2, and the Codex provider's codex_websocket_url/1, turn the provider base URL into a wss:// URL and start ReqLLM.Streaming.WebSocketSession with an authorization header that carries the OpenAI API key or the OAuth access token.

2. Missing TLS options. WebSocketSession.init/1 passes only the headers and the timeouts to WebSocketSession.Client.start/3, and the allowlist in start/3 forwards only name, debug, async, handle_initial_conn_failure, and the socket timeouts to WebSockex.start/4. cna.title: RIOT: nanocoap_fileserver ignores response initialization failure, leading to reachable assertion

descriptions.value: RIOT is an open-source microcontroller operating system designed for Internet of Things devices and other embedded systems. From version 2023.07 through version 2026.07, nanocoap_fileserver callers in sys/net/application_layer/nanocoap/fileserver.c ignore a failure returned by _resp_init() when coap_build_reply() cannot fit a response header into the response buffer. A remote client can send a CoAP request with a sufficiently large extended token when nanocoap_token_ext is enabled, causing response initialization to fail while _get_file() or _get_directory() continues with stale response state. The path then reaches _calc_szx2() and its pdu->payload_len > reserve assertion, terminating the affected service or device task. No fixed release is available as of this review.

cna.title: OWASP Coraza WAF: ProcessURI silently drops QUERY_STRING and ARGS_GET on URI parse failure — defense-in-depth bypass for non-net/http integrations

descriptions.value: OWASP Coraza WAF is a golang modsecurity compatible web application firewall library. From 3.0.0 until 3.8.0, ProcessURI in internal/corazawaf/transaction.go handles a url.ParseRequestURI failure by retaining the raw URI but leaving QUERY_STRING, ARGS_GET, ARGS_GET_NAMES, and the GET-derived portion of ARGS empty. descriptions.value: x64dbg-MCP Server is a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) plugin for x64dbg that exposes the debugger's full functionality over HTTP. Prior to 1.2, src/core/mcp_server.zig parses an unbounded Content-Length value in parseContentLength() and uses it in unchecked usize addition in wsRecv() before token authentication. The server listens on 0.0.0.0 by default in affected versions. An unauthenticated network client can supply a near-maximum Content-Length value to trigger a runtime integer-overflow panic in Debug and ReleaseSafe builds, terminating the entire x64dbg process and its live debugging session. cna.title: MISP Correlation Engine Fails to Refresh When Event Distribution or Sharing Group Changes

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [correlation] fix correlation distribution refresh on

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [correlation] fix correlation distribution refresh on
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix ensures that the before-save hook retrieves the previously persisted distribution and sharing_group_id values from the database for existing events, rather than capturing the incoming (new) data. This allows the after-save logic to correctly detect when these fields have changed and trigger a correlation refresh, ensuring access boundaries on correlated data are enforced promptly.
assumptions: The exact fixed version number is not specified in the patch metadata; the tag boundary indicates the fix is 47 commits after v2.5.48, but the release tag containing this commit is unknown.
The security impact is assessed as limited information disclosure through stale correlations; the patch does not indicate a direct privilege escalation or data corruption vector.
CAPEC-114 (Parameter Tampering) is the closest available mapping; no CAPEC specifically covers 'stale derived data after a legitimate parameter change' and the mapping is approximate.

The assumption that the afterSave hook uses __beforeSaveData to compare old vs new distribution/sharing_group_id values is inferred from the commit message and the code change pattern; the afterSave code itself is not included in the patch.
CVSS UI:N assumes the stale correlation data is accessible via the normal MISP UI/API without additional user interaction beyond the initial event edit.
The Co-Authored-By line for Claude Opus 4.8 is treated as a tool credit, not a human remediation developer.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Event.php, the beforeSave method was modified. Previously, $this->__beforeSaveData was set to the full incoming $this->data['Event'] array. The patch replaces this with: (1) initializing __beforeSaveData to null, (2) checking whether the event has an existing id (i.e., it is an update, not a create), (3) issuing a targeted database query (recursive -1, selecting only Event.distribution and Event.sharing_group_id) to fetch the currently stored values, and (4) storing those fetched values in __beforeSaveData. This ensures the after-save comparison correctly identifies distribution/sharing_group_id changes.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L: An authenticated user simply edits an event's sharing group; no race condition or complex setup is needed. AT:N: No manipulation of a separate attack target is required. PR:L: Requires an authenticated user with write access to events. UI:N: The stale correlation persists without further user interaction. VC/VI/VA:N: The vulnerable component (the event save logic) is not directly compromised in confidentiality, integrity, or availability. SC:L: The security impact is on the broader MISP instance: users in a broader sharing group may see correlation data referencing an event that was moved to a more restrictive group, resulting in limited information disclosure. SI/SA:N: No integrity or safety impact on other systems.

capecRationale.rationale: The closest plausible CAPEC is Parameter Tampering: a user modifies the distribution or sharing_group_id parameters of an event, and the application fails to properly enforce the resulting access-control changes on correlated data. The mapping is uncertain because this is not a malicious tamper per se but a legitimate parameter modification that exposes a system defect; however, CAPEC-114 best captures the scenario where parameter changes are not properly reflected in downstream access enforcement. No more specific CAPEC for 'stale derived data after parameter change' exists in the CAPEC catalog.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The core security impact is that correlation data access boundaries are not enforced when an event's sharing group or distribution changes. Stale correlations can expose event data to users who should no longer have access, constituting an improper access control failure.

The root cause is that the __beforeSaveData variable was initialized with the incoming (new) data rather than the previously stored data, causing the change-detection logic in afterSave to fail. This is a classic improper initialization of a state variable used for change detection.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-114 Parameter Tampering

solutions.value: The fix ensures that the before-save hook retrieves the previously persisted distribution and sharing_group_id values from the database for existing events, rather than capturing the incoming (new) data. This allows the after-save logic to correctly detect when these fields have changed and trigger a correlation refresh, ensuring access boundaries on correlated data are enforced promptly.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a defect in its event save workflow that prevents the correlation engine from recalculating correlations when an event's distribution level or sharing group is modified.

When a user edits an existing event and changes its distribution or sharing_group_id, the internal before-save hook stored the incoming (new) data rather than the previously persisted values. As a result, the after-save comparison that determines whether a correlation refresh is needed never detected the change, and stale correlations persisted.

Security impact:

- Stale correlations may continue to expose event data to users in a broader sharing group after the event has been moved to a more restrictive group, resulting in unintended information disclosure.

- Conversely, newly relevant correlations may not appear after a distribution widening, degrading the completeness of threat intelligence sharing.

Preconditions:

- An authenticated user with write access to at least one MISP event.

- The user modifies the event's distribution or sharing_group_id field.

Affected versions: <2.5.48

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. Decrypt passes attacker-controlled EncryptionInfo and EncryptedPackage data into standardDecrypt or agileDecrypt before validating the structures used by those routines. When a malformed OLE compound file with a version-valid EncryptionInfo stream is opened or passed to Decrypt, nine malformed-input classes reach unrecovered Go runtime panics instead of the documented error path, allowing an attacker to terminate the calling process. descriptions.value: The AsyncHttpClient (AHC) library allows Java applications to easily execute HTTP requests and asynchronously process HTTP responses. Prior to 3.0.12 and 2.16.1, a proxied ws request is carried through CONNECT, but NettyRequestFactory.newNettyRequest and requestUri decide whether to attach proxy authentication and an absolute-form target only from whether the URI is secure. Because ws is not marked secure, the tunneled WebSocket upgrade sent to the origin includes the proxy's Proxy-Authorization value. Basic credentials are directly recoverable and Digest responses can be replayed or cracked offline. This issue is fixed in versions 3.0.12 and 2.16.1.

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, whose report readers cut the leading blank lines off once. Until then, turn bounce processing, complaint processing and list management off (the default).

descriptions.value: Inefficient algorithmic complexity in the bounce and complaint processing of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 and 6.3.5 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to stop mail delivery by sending messages, when bounce processing or complaint processing is enabled or a mailing list is managed by the server (none is by default). The readers of incoming delivery status notifications (RFC 3464) and abuse feedback reports (RFC 5965) removed the blank lines at the start of the returned headers part two bytes at a time, copying the rest of the part each time, so their work grew with the square of the number of blank lines. A message shaped like such a report, whose headers part begins with a very large number of blank lines within the reader's 2 MB limit, keeps a delivery thread busy for over a minute while it is delivered, and a few such messages a minute keep every delivery thread busy.

Authorization metadata is stored per row in tl_search, but disabling the setting removes the protected-row filter without deleting rows indexed while protection was enabled. The protected pages continue to return an authorization response, so this issue exposes search metadata and indexed text rather than bypassing page access. This issue is fixed in versions 5.3.50 and 5.7.12.

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.1.0 to 2.11.0, a Zip64 uncompressed size with the high bit set is converted from uint64 to a negative int64 before signed size-limit checks and allocation. cna.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which parses the FETCH command and runs the server's case-insensitive string operations in a single pass, reads each SEARCH and UID set and HEADER.FIELDS list once per command, substitutes the saved-result marker once, and refuses a FETCH whose sections add up to many times the message before sending any. There is no configuration workaround; the commands require only a signed-in account. Restricting IMAP access to trusted accounts and networks reduces who can send them.

descriptions.value: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 processes several IMAP commands from a signed-in account in time quadratic in the command's length or in the number of elements it names, and can be made to hold memory out of proportion to a command. The FETCH data-item parser normalised a BODY[] section with a case-insensitive string replacement that copied the whole item per occurrence and split the item list by repeatedly copying the remainder of the command; the server's case-insensitive search compared a needle afresh at every position, so a long SEARCH TEXT key over a message cost the product of the two lengths; SEARCH message sets and the saved-result marker ($), SORT criteria, HEADER.FIELDS name lists and UID ranges were each read once per message rather than once per command; and a FETCH naming a message's sections very many times read and held every section in memory before sending any. An IMAP command may continue past one line through non-synchronizing literals, so one command can reach about eleven megabytes. The IMAP worker threads are a small pool shared with SMTP and POP3, so a signed-in user sending such commands can make the IMAP, SMTP and POP3 services stop responding (CWE-407) and can consume excessive memory (CWE-400).

cna.title: Strawberry GraphQL: Synchronous permission checks can treat an awaitable authorization result as truthy

descriptions.value: Strawberry GraphQL is a library for creating GraphQL APIs. From 0.217.0 until 0.326.1, PermissionExtension.resolve() on a synchronous field resolver evaluates the result of has_permission() for truthiness. When a custom permission declares has_permission() as a normal function but returns an awaitable, supports_sync does not classify it as asynchronous, the awaitable is not awaited, and its inherently truthy object value permits the protected resolver to run even when the result would resolve to false. This affects synchronous field resolvers under both execute_sync() and execute(); permissions declared with async def has_permission() and synchronous permissions returning a boolean are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.326.1.

workarounds.value:
--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to ensure slash delimiter separation when joining the management root path with permission rules in quarkus-vertx-http to prevent authorization bypass on management endpoints: upgrade to the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds, which inserts a slash delimiter when concatenating the management root path with relative permission rules so policies bind to actual endpoints rather than malformed paths, closing direct HTTP requests to exposed management paths. Until patched, this is a concern on Quarkus applications exposing the management interface to local or private network callers across all platforms, so restrict network and local access to the Quarkus management interface to trusted administrators, preventing untrusted callers from reaching exposed endpoints. As a compensating measure, restrict network access to the port exposing the Quarkus management interface using host-based firewalls such as firewalld or nftables and record administrative actions executed through the management interface and forward logs to a SIEM to detect unauthorized configuration changes. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying improper path concatenation defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-909 Default-Deny API Authorization Policy (high)

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the management interface of the Quarkus framework, specifically within the quarkus-vertx-http component. The issue occurs when the framework incorrectly combines the management root path with specific permission rules, leading to a situation where security policies are applied to the wrong internal paths. As a result, an attacker can bypass intended authorization checks and gain unauthorized access to sensitive management endpoints.

cna.title: amqp091-go: Pre-negotiation frame limit is not enforced to 4KB

descriptions.value: amqp091-go is a Go AMQP 0.9.1 client. From 1.13.0 until 1.14.0, the frame-size mitigation from the prior allocation advisory can be bypassed before connection.tune completes because Connection.maxFrameSize uses zero for both the not-yet-negotiated and negotiated-unlimited states. A malicious or compromised AMQP peer can send a short body-frame header with a large declared payload length, causing ReadFrame and the body-frame parser to allocate attacker-selected memory before the payload is received or the frame's protocol state is rejected. The condition is reachable through public Open even when Config.FrameSize is set to the protocol minimum and can cause severe memory pressure, out-of-memory termination, or loss of the client process before authentication completes. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.0.

cna.title: fast-jwt: createVerifier accepts unsigned JWTs when key is '' or null and algorithms is explicitly set

descriptions.value: fast-jwt provides fast JSON Web Token (JWT) implementation. Prior to 6.3.1, fast-jwt createVerifier accepts an unsigned JWT when key is an empty string or null and algorithms is a non-empty allowlist. Falsy synchronous keys bypass prepareKeyOrSecret, allowedAlgorithms remains active, hasKey is false, and the empty signature avoids the verifySignature gate. An attacker can therefore submit a token containing arbitrary claims without possessing a signing key, resulting in authentication or authorization bypass. Claim validators still run, and non-empty keys, an empty key without algorithms, and the async key resolver path do not have this behavior. This issue is fixed in version 6.3.1.

Opening a crafted LIT file that reaches one of these variants can cause invalid pointer reads and deterministic application termination. No broader impact is claimed beyond the advisory-supported conditions. No fixed version is available as of this review.

From 7.0.0 until 9.4.0, reactive applications generated with Spring WebFlux, Spring Data R2DBC, and a SQL database pass the attacker-controlled sort request parameter from paginated entity-list endpoints into createOrderByFields in generators/spring-boot/generators/data-relational/templates/src/main/java/package/repository/EntityManager_reactive.java.ejs. cna.title: Gallery Custom Links <= 2.3.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Author Display Name + Comment HTML Comment Body

descriptions.value: The Gallery Custom Links plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display_name (profile.php) + comment (wp-comments-post.php)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires two coordinated inputs from the same authenticated attacker: an HTML comment payload stored in a comment body (preserved verbatim by WordPress comment kses) and a matching simple_html_dom noise key placed in the attacker's display_name (which survives esc_attr() intact), with substitution occurring after both filters have run during the plugin's default-on output-buffering pass over the full rendered page.
