cna.title: Integer overflow causes an infinite loop in message buffer growth in PgBouncer

credits.value: Thanks to Brian Cosgrove (@cosgroveb) for finding and reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Set max_packet_size to 2147483647 (the default) or lower.

descriptions.value: Integer overflow in the message buffer growth logic (mbuf_make_room) in PgBouncer 1.21.0 through 1.26.0 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service when max_packet_size is configured above 2147483648. A packet header declaring a length above 2^31 makes the buffer size computation overflow, leaving the growth loop unable to terminate. Because PgBouncer serves all clients from a single process, this saturates a CPU core and stalls every pooled connection until the process is restarted. Since 1.23.0 the overflow is reachable before authentication with a five-byte packet header.

descriptions.description: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

configurations.value: max_packet_size is set to 2147483649 or higher. The default max_packet_size of 2147483647 is not affected.

cna.title: Excelize: a row whose earlier cell has a higher column reference than its last cell panics index out of range on almost every worksheet read API

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.0.0 to 2.11.0, checkRow sizes its target cell slice from the last cell in XML document order and then re-scatters every cell by its explicit column reference. GetCellValue reaches workSheetReader and checkRow, where targetList is too short for an earlier out-of-order cell. When a crafted row places a higher-column cell before a lower-column final cell and a non-streaming worksheet API reads the sheet, the earlier cell's column index exceeds the slice length derived from the final cell, allowing an attacker to cause an unrecovered panic and terminate the process. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: SumatraPDF: `sumatrapdfrestrict.ini` never revokes any permission (fail-open policy initialization)

descriptions.value: SumatraPDF is a multi-format reader for Windows. In 3.6.1 and earlier, InitializePolicies() starts the sumatrapdfrestrict.ini path with gPolicyRestrictions set to Perm::All and only ORs permission bits, so the INI file never revokes permissions. Deploying SumatraPDF with this INI file, including a malformed file or zero-valued permission settings, can silently bypass configured disk, network, printing, registry, clipboard, preference, and fullscreen restrictions. The -restrict command-line path works correctly and is not affected. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: fast-jwt clockTolerance: Infinity silently bypasses both exp and nbf validation (and persists in the verifier cache)

descriptions.value: fast-jwt provides fast JSON Web Token (JWT) implementation. Prior to 6.3.0, fast-jwt createVerifier accepts Infinity for clockTolerance because its option validation checks type and negativity but not finiteness. In validateClaimDateValue, infinite positive and negative modifiers make exp and nbf comparisons always pass, allowing expired or not-yet-active tokens to be accepted. The verifier cache also derives infinite bounds, so entries created under this configuration can remain valid until eviction. Exploitation requires an application administrator or equivalent configuration path to set clockTolerance to Infinity. This issue is fixed in version 6.3.0.

The driver's server-monitoring path contains panic recovery and is limited to server-selection failure.

cna.title: Source-to-image: source-to-image: security boundary bypass via absolute symbolic link extraction

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Yashashree Gund for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Treat s2i builder images and application source as trusted inputs. Do not run s2i-based builds against builder images or repositories you do not control or have not verified.

Where possible, run builds on isolated build nodes and restrict who can trigger builds or change BuildConfig and image stream references that point at custom builder images.

There is no configuration option to disable only this symlink extraction behavior without changing how builds are performed. Apply updated source-to-image packages or rebuilt platform images when Red Hat publishes them for your product and stream.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in source-to-image. When unpacking archive files, the application fails to properly sanitize symbolic links pointing to absolute file paths. An attacker who supplies a malicious builder image can exploit this vulnerability by embedding links pointing outside the extraction directory. This allows the attacker to bypass sandbox boundaries, potentially leading to unauthorized information disclosure or file modification on the host system.

cna.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, in which each account or administrator holds at most fifty sessions and gives up its own least recently used one, and a full table makes room out of the sessions of whoever holds the most. Until then: limit the rate of POST /api/v1/session per client at a reverse proxy in front of the listener, and disable an account found signing in repeatedly (its sign-ins are in the application log and its device list).

descriptions.value: Uncontrolled eviction in the browser session table of the REST API in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.28 through 6.3.5 allows a remote authenticated user to end other users' sessions. The table of browser sessions, shared by every account, the server administrator and support sessions, dropped its least recently used session whenever it was full, whoever it belonged to, and placed no limit on how many sessions one account could hold. A user who repeatedly signs in with their own mailbox password can therefore keep the table full and sign out every webmail and administration session that is idle for more than a short time, for as long as they continue.

descriptions.description: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

cna.title: Discussion Board <= 2.6.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via User Profile Website (user_url) Field

descriptions.value: The Discussion Board – WordPress Forum Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 via the user profile Website (user_url) field. This is due to insufficient output escaping in the ctdb_filter_comment_author_name() callback hooked to get_comment_author_link, which interpolates the raw user_url value into a single-quoted href attribute without esc_url() or esc_attr(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses a Discussion Board topic containing the attacker's reply.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

cna.title: msgpack5: Quadratic parsing in the streaming decoder

descriptions.value: msgpack5 is a msgpack v5 implementation for node.js and the browser. Prior to 6.1.0, the streaming decoder reparses an incomplete array or map from the beginning whenever another chunk arrives. A remote peer can split one valid MessagePack container across many small chunks, causing completed elements to be decoded repeatedly, producing quadratic CPU use and blocking the event loop. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.0.

cna.title: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which matches a ':matches' pattern by placing each piece once (time linear in the value times the pattern) and removes 'deleteheader' fields in one pass. Until then, review active Sieve scripts for ':matches' patterns with several wildcards and for 'deleteheader', and lower the maximum message size.

descriptions.value: Inefficient complexity in the Sieve filter evaluation of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.24 through 6.3.5 allows an authenticated account holder to make the mail services unavailable with their own filter. A ':matches' pattern was matched by a backtracking descent whose time grew with the matched value's length raised to the number of wildcards, so a pattern such as '*a*a*a*b' over 800 characters took 44 seconds; and 'deleteheader' erased the fields it removed one at a time, so removing many fields of one name over a message's header cost O(N^2) (80,000 fields took 18.8 seconds). Sieve filters run on the small, shared delivery thread pool, so an account holder whose active script does this, fed a few messages they can send themselves, empties the pool and stops delivery for the whole server. The script is the account holder's own and cannot be set for another user.

cna.title: Jivejdon through commit ee67a65e Missing Rate Limiting via /account/smsVRAction SMS Endpoint

descriptions.value: Jivejdon from commit e0306088 through commit ee67a65e lacks rate limiting on the unauthenticated /account/smsVRAction endpoint handled by SmsQQAction, allowing unlimited SMS sending. Attackers can load newAccount.jsp to set session attributes, then repeatedly call the endpoint to harass arbitrary phone numbers and exhaust the operator's Tencent Cloud SMS balance.

cna.title: fast-jwt : Silent claim-validator bypass when JWT payload is a JSON array

descriptions.description: CWE-1287: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input

descriptions.value: fast-jwt provides fast JSON Web Token (JWT) implementation. Prior to 6.3.0, fast-jwt createVerifier accepts a validly signed JWT whose payload is a JSON array because src/decoder.js checks that the payload is an object but does not reject arrays. The claim validator loop then finds no named exp, nbf, iss, aud, sub, jti, or nonce properties and silently skips those configured checks, returning the array as a successfully verified payload. An attacker who can produce or influence a validly signed token may bypass expiry, issuer, audience, subject, revocation, and replay protections. The opt-in requiredClaims option can block missing claims, and signature verification itself is not bypassed. This issue is fixed in version 6.3.0.

cna.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in the Highcharts Library Bundled with Vaadin Charts

descriptions.value: CAPEC-63 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CAPEC-77 Manipulating User-Controlled Variables

solutions.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

supportingMedia.value: Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade.

workarounds.value: Do not pass data the application does not control to the chart configuration. That covers the additionalOptions property of <vaadin-chart> and <vaadin-chart-series>, updateConfiguration() and the configuration property, setKeys() and addKey() on the PlotOptions classes, Credits.setUnsafeHref(), and the text options that accept markup such as Title.setText(), Subtitle.setText(), axis labels, data labels and tooltip formats. descriptions.value:

cna.title: Incorrect Default Permissions in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7. Its hMailServer.exe /ProtectFolders, which setup runs at the end of every server installation and upgrade, gives the program folder, Bin and ControlPanel SYSTEM and the Administrators full control and Users read and execute (where every user could read the folder), nothing inherited, and, where another account owned one of them, makes the Administrators its owner and takes away that folder's own entries that let others change it; setup also gives a program folder it creates those permissions before it copies anything into it, and hardens, before its files, the existing folder of an installation of the Control Panel alone. 6.3.7 does not yet create a new program folder with those permissions already in place, harden the folder before setup's own steps on an upgrade, a repair or a server installation into a folder that already existed, refuse a link or junction on the program folder's path (it is logged), or list the files in Bin and ControlPanel by owner. Before upgrading an affected installation, or until it is upgraded, follow from an elevated Command Prompt the steps in the hMailServer documentation, ServiceAccount.md, "Before upgrading an installation at a drive's root": first note who owns the program folder and what is directly in it (dir /q /a "<folder>") and everything in Bin, ControlPanel, Events, WebAdmin, DBScripts, Addons and Languages (dir /q /s /a); then, for the program folder, then Bin, then ControlPanel, make the Administrators its owner (icacls "<folder>" /setowner *S-1-5-32-544, the folder alone, without /T); take away every entry of the folder's own but SYSTEM's, the Administrators' and deny entries, one account a line (icacls "<folder>" /remove:g: the Users' and the service's by their SIDs, the service's only where the server is installed; the two application package groups by theirs, *S-1-15-2-1 and *S-1-15-2-2; anybody else's by the name icacls lists; and an entry icacls lists by a SID that names no account with the documentation's PowerShell line); replace what it inherits (icacls "<folder>" /inheritance:r /grant:r *S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-545:(OI)(CI)RX); and on Bin and ControlPanel, where the server is installed, give the service account back its read and execute - each icacls line reporting "Successfully processed 1 files"; or move the installation under Program Files. Reinstall the programs into a new folder that only the administrators may change, not over the installation, where accounts that are not administrators could sign in while the installation was exposed, where another account made the program folder or could change it before the installation, where anybody but SYSTEM, the Administrators or TrustedInstaller owned the program folder, a file directly in it, or Bin, ControlPanel, Events, WebAdmin, DBScripts, Addons or Languages or anything in them, or where one of the three folders had an entry of its own that let another account change it, or one the steps could not take away: setup leaves in place every file it does not ship, and puts the event script, which the service runs, and the scripts in Addons only where none is there, so read the old event script before copying it. Setup run into a folder without a settings file sets up a new, empty server there, so the settings file and the data go into the new folder first (ServiceAccount.md, "Reinstalling into a new folder"): stop the service and run nothing from the old folder, its uninstaller included; copy, not move, the mail, the built-in database's folder and the settings file into the new folder, the copies kept private; read the copy of the settings file, deleting its AdministratorPassword and each [Directories] line with a path in the old folder; then, with a 32-bit installation's uninstall entry taken away, run the release's setup with the new folder; read in the new Control Panel the programs the database's settings name, make the REST API's keys again, change each path the database holds into the old folder, and, once nothing names it, delete the old folder by hand.

descriptions.value: Incorrect default permissions in the Windows installer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allow a local authenticated user to run code as the mail server's high-privileged accounts when the product is installed in a folder whose permissions are inherited from a writable parent, such as the root of a drive. The installer places the server's programs in the Bin folder of the program folder and gives neither the program folder nor Bin any permissions of their own, so they inherit the parent's. Under the default location, Program Files, ordinary users receive only read and execute and the configuration is not affected; but the installer accepts any path without warning, and a program folder at the root of an NTFS volume inherits write access for a broad group - Authenticated Users (Modify) on a Windows client, Users (create files and folders) on Windows Server. A local user without administrator rights can then alter or replace the service program, which runs as LocalSystem or as the service's virtual account, or the programs an administrator runs elevated from Bin during setup and maintenance, or place a library in Bin that those programs load in place of the system copy, gaining code execution with those privileges. The default Program Files installation is not affected.

cna.title: Pre-authentication heap out-of-bounds write in FalkorDB Bolt BoltReadHandler via RESET message

descriptions.value: A heap-based out-of-bounds write in the BoltReadHandler function (src/bolt/bolt_api.c) in FalkorDB before 4.20.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code by sending a Bolt RESET message with an attacker-chosen chunk size to the Bolt port. The handler checks the size only with ASSERT(), which is compiled out in release builds, then computes a destination pointer from the wire-supplied 16-bit size and moves buffered data up to about 64 KiB backwards past the start of the read buffer. Only deployments that enable the Bolt endpoint (BOLT_PORT, disabled by default) are affected.

solutions.value: Upgrade FalkorDB to version 4.20.0 or later. Bolt protocol support, including the code affected by this issue, was removed in 4.20.0.

workarounds.value: Leave the Bolt endpoint disabled (do not set the BOLT_PORT module configuration; it is disabled by default), or restrict network access to the Bolt port to trusted clients.

cna.title: Missing Authorization in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which uses a Sieve notify :from only when it is an address that reaches the account (the account's own address or an active alias of it) - otherwise the notification goes from the account's own address, logged - and refuses a notify :from that is not an address when the script is stored, as the vacation action already does; and which sends a reply of an account's or a domain's mail rule only from an address the rule's owner may send as, refusing any other when the rule is saved and not sending a reply stored with one before (logged). Until then, where accounts need not set Sieve scripts, close the script surfaces: keep ManageSieve off (ManageSieveServerPort=0, the default) or bound to the loopback, and turn the REST API off where the webmail's filter editor is not wanted (RestApiPort=0, the default); and review active Sieve scripts for a notify whose :from is not the account's own address or an alias of it, and account and domain rules for a reply from an address the rule's owner may not send as. There is no per-extension setting that turns notify off while Sieve is in use.

descriptions.value: Missing authorization in the Sieve notify action (6.2.22 through 6.3.6) and in the mail-rule Reply action (6.0.0 through 6.3.6) of Progressive Robot hMailServer allows an authenticated user to send mail through the server as any address. A Sieve notify sends a notification message, and its :from tag names the sender; the server set the notification's From header to that :from as the script wrote it, without checking that the address belongs to the account - the check that the Sieve vacation action applies to its own :from, and that the server applies to the sender of mail queued over COM or sent from the webmail. An account that can store a Sieve script (over ManageSieve, the REST API's self-service filter, or the administration interface) could therefore have the server send a notification from any address, on this server or anywhere; and where the claimed address is at a domain the server hosts with DKIM signing enabled, the server signed the notification with that domain's DKIM key, because it signs by the From header's domain, producing forged mail aligned to pass the domain's DMARC policy. The notify action and this behaviour were introduced in 6.2.22. In the mail-rule engine, a rule's Reply was likewise sent from whatever address the action named, whoever the rule belonged to, so that an account acting on its own rules over COM, a domain administrator, or an API key confined to a domain (over the REST API from 6.3.4) could have a domain's or an account's rule reply from any address, signed, where that address is at a domain the server hosts with DKIM signing enabled, with that domain's key.

cna.title: Apache CXF: The attachment header size and count limits can be bypassed, which allows denial of service through memory exhaustion.

descriptions.value:
In Apache CXF, the parser for multipart/MTOM attachment part headers did not fully enforce the configured attachment-max-header-size (default 300 characters) and attachment-headers-max-count (default 500) limits. The size limit was applied only to each physical line, not to a header value built from continuation lines or to the combined values of a repeated header. The count limit was checked against the number of distinct header names, not the total number of header lines. A remote, unauthenticated attacker could send a multipart request with very large folded or repeated part headers. The server would then allocate memory without bound, causing a denial of service. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

solutions.value:
IBM strongly recommends addressing the vulnerability now by upgrading  Langflow OSS to version 1.12.5. https://pypi.org/project/langflow/1.12.5/ 



For Langflow OSS versions 1.0.0 - 1.12.4, follow the  Prepare to upgrade instructions and release-specific configuration changes https://docs.langflow.org/release-notes , including backing up your existing installation, then follow the  Langflow OSS installation instructions https://docs.langflow.org/get-started-installation  to install version 1.12.5 and test your flows. For deployments using MCP stdio, also apply the configuration controls in Workarounds and Mitigations.



This bulletin also discloses fixes delivered in prior releases: CVE-2026-107366 was fixed in version 1.9.0; CVE-2026-18894 was fixed in version 1.11.2; and CVE-2026-77817 was fixed in version 1.11.5. Version 1.12.5 includes these fixes.

supportingMedia.value:

For Langflow OSS versions 1.0.0 - 1.12.4, follow the Prepare to upgrade instructions and release-specific configuration changes, including backing up your existing installation, then follow the Langflow OSS installation instructions to install version 1.12.5 and test your flows. For deployments using MCP stdio, also apply the configuration controls in Workarounds and Mitigations.

This bulletin also discloses fixes delivered in prior releases: CVE-2026-107366 was fixed in version 1.9.0; CVE-2026-18894 was fixed in version 1.11.2; and CVE-2026-77817 was fixed in version 1.11.5. Version 1.12.5 includes these fixes.

workarounds.value:
IBM strongly recommends applying the following configuration controls to deployments using MCP stdio in addition to upgrading Langflow OSS to version 1.12.5. These controls do not replace the upgrade.



Set LANGFLOW_MCP_SERVER_INTERPRETER_HARDENING=true to reject direct shell-script execution, and set LANGFLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENT_ADMIN_ONLY=true to block non-admin MCP stdio access. Restart the Langflow service after updating its environment configuration. These restrictions can require changes to existing MCP server launch configurations and limit which users can use MCP stdio.



For public workflows, retain the default restriction on custom components. Explicitly enabling LANGFLOW_ALLOW_PUBLIC_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS permits custom component execution and changes the default protection described for CVE-2026-18894.



For CVE-2026-77817, upgrading prevents the identified secret disclosure in new flow and project exports. Revoke or rotate any credentials exposed in previously exported files; upgrading does not remove secrets from copies already exported.

cna.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: unauthenticated cpu exhaustion via saml 1.1 keyinfo infinite loop

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the SAML 1.1 XML parsing logic of Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when the parser encounters unexpected elements within a security token's key information section, causing the processing thread to enter an infinite loop. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted requests, leading to 100% CPU usage and a total denial of service that requires a server restart to resolve.

cna.x_redhatCweChain: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition

workarounds.value:
Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to ensure the StAX-based XML parser in keycloak-saml-core advances the cursor or rejects unhandled child elements when parsing ds:KeyInfo in SAML 1.1 tokens: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4.17, 26.6.8 (or the fixed Rhbk/Keycloak Rhel/Keycloak Services builds), which advances the cursor or rejects unexpected child elements within ds:KeyInfo rather than repeatedly peeking without advancing the parser, closing crafted SAML 1.1 request containing unexpected ds:KeyInfo child elements. Until patched, this is a concern on Keycloak deployments exposing unauthenticated SAML endpoints, so Restrict network access to Keycloak SAML endpoints such as /realms/{realm}/protocol/saml to trusted clients. As a compensating measure, Configure systemd service watchdogs (WatchdogSec and Restart) to monitor responsiveness and automatically restart Keycloak when worker threads hang and Implement rate limiting and connection throttling on unauthenticated HTTP requests targeting Keycloak SAML endpoints to mitigate thread exhaustion. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying infinite-loop XML parsing defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1204 Service Watchdog and Automatic Restart (systemd WatchdogSec/Restart) (medium)

cna.title: Pydantic AI: Concurrency-limited models can keep their slot when a streamed request ends early

descriptions.description: CWE-772: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime

descriptions.value: Pydantic AI is a Python agent framework for building applications and workflows with Generative AI. From 2.10.0 until 2.53.0, streamed requests made through ConcurrencyLimitedModel or limit_model_concurrency can retain shared concurrency slots because anyio.CapacityLimiter associates an acquired slot with the borrowing task while streaming cleanup can run in a different task. Early stream termination, cancellation, consumer exceptions, or complete stream_text() consumption with debounce_by=0.1 can therefore leave capacity occupied, eventually preventing later requests that share the long-lived limiter from proceeding and causing a denial of service. Agent-level max_concurrency and non-streaming model requests are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 2.53.0.

cna.title: Use of Less Trusted Source in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7. It records on each message, and on every copy of it, whether the message came from outside: an SMTP session that did not authenticate and was not a submission the server's IP ranges allow without authentication, a download from an external account, or an imported file. It signs a message as its From domain only when an authenticated user submitted it (as another domain the server hosts only when the account may send as the address its From names), the server made it, or an IP range let it in as one of the server's own domains, so mail from outside and its forwards keep only the signatures they arrived with, and a signed-in account's message from an address at another hosted domain that the account may not send as is sent unsigned as that domain. Until then, do one of the following: publish a DMARC policy of quarantine or reject for each hosted domain the server signs for and set the server's DMARC failure score (DMARCFailureScore) at or above the spam delete threshold (SpamDeleteThreshold), so that such a message is refused on arrival; refuse it in an OnAcceptMessage event script when the client has not authenticated and the From header names a domain the server signs for; remove the forwards, rule forwards, Sieve redirects, alias and list members and mirror addresses that carry mail to outside addresses; or disable DKIM signing for the hosted domains, which alone of these also covers a signed-in account's submission. Rotate the DKIM key of any domain whose key may have signed forged mail.

descriptions.value: Use of a less trusted source in the DKIM signing of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to have mail they write signed with the DKIM key of a domain the server hosts, so that it passes DKIM and DMARC for that domain at other receivers. With DKIM signing enabled for a hosted domain, the server signed every message on its first delivery pass as the domain named in its From header, before local delivery, whatever the message's origin and without checking that its sender had authenticated. A sender anywhere could therefore send the server, as ordinary inbound mail, a message whose From is any address at such a domain, and the server signed it with that domain's key. Every copy the server then sent on to an address outside carried a valid signature aligned with the forged From, whatever the domain's DMARC policy: an account's forward, a mail rule's forward or copy, a Sieve redirect, an alias or distribution list with an outside member, the mirror copy, a managed-list or journal copy, or a message released from quarantine. A signed copy can also be re-sent to other recipients while the domain's key is unchanged. Exploitation needs DKIM signing to be enabled for the hosted domain (it is off until configured) and, for the forgery to leave the server, a forward, alias, list or rule that carries the domain's mail to an outside address. The signer likewise signed a message submitted over authenticated SMTP as whatever hosted domain its From header named, a header authenticated SMTP does not hold to the submitting account, so that an account of one hosted domain could have mail written in the name of another hosted domain signed with that domain's key; this mattered where the server holds signed-in senders to their own envelope addresses (SmtpAuthenticatedSenderCheck, off by default), as the signature was then the remaining way for such mail to pass the other domain's DMARC policy.

cna.title: BuddyForms <= 2.10.5 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Form-Type Confusion via 'bf_post_type' Parameter

descriptions.value: The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.5 via a form-type confusion attack through the `bf_post_type` parameter. This is due to the public frontend submission handler `buddyforms_form_response_no_ajax()` authorizing logged-out submissions based solely on the target form's `public_submit` flag while independently trusting the attacker-supplied `$_POST['bf_post_type']` to determine the post type of the newly created object — a cross-check introduced in 2.10.2 applies only to existing posts (`post_id != 0`) and is completely bypassed for new-object creation — combined with the `save_post` listener `buddyforms_edit_form_save_meta_box_data()` lacking both a `current_user_can()` capability check and a form-builder nonce, causing it to unconditionally persist attacker-supplied `$_POST['buddyforms_options']` for any newly inserted `buddyforms` CPT post. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert a rogue BuddyForms form configuration with an attacker-controlled `new_user_role` value into the live global form registry, then submit a registration through that form to create a new WordPress account with administrator-level privileges and achieve full site takeover. Exploitation requires the WordPress site to have "Anyone can register" enabled and at least one public BuddyForms form attached to a page, both of which are standard BuddyForms deployment configurations.

cna.title: Excelize: Unbounded <col max> attribute is loaded with no MaxColumns check and expanded per-column by flatCols(), so any column mutator hangs or OOMs the process

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.1.0 to 2.11.0, flatCols expands file-loaded column ranges without validating Min and Max against the worksheet column limit. SetColWidth reaches flatCols, which expands xlsxCol.Min through xlsxCol.Max without enforcing MaxColumns. When a crafted worksheet supplies an oversized col max attribute and the application invokes a column mutator, flatCols performs a deep copy and append for every attacker-selected column number, allowing an attacker to consume excessive CPU and memory or trigger OOM. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: Cyrus-sasl: heap buffer overflow in cyrus-sasl add_to_challenge() allows malicious server to crash or compromise digest-md5 clients

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Bruno Fournier and Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

workarounds.value:
If DIGEST-MD5 authentication is not strictly required, remove the optional cyrus-sasl-md5 package to eliminate the vulnerable plugin:

# dnf remove cyrus-sasl-md5

Alternatively, configure client applications to disable DIGEST-MD5 and HTTP Digest authentication methods, prioritizing stronger mechanisms such as GSSAPI or SCRAM.

Caveat: Removing cyrus-sasl-md5 removes support for both DIGEST-MD5 and CRAM-MD5 mechanisms. Any client or server process depending on these algorithms will fail to negotiate authentication. Active services utilizing SASL may need to be restarted to unload the plugin from memory.

descriptions.value: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL. The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin computes the size of the buffer needed for a challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a crash of the client application.

cna.title: Mechanize sends credential headers to another origin after a meta refresh

descriptions.value: The Mechanize library is used for automating interaction with websites. Prior to 2.14.1, Mechanize applies no origin trust boundary in Mechanize::HTTP::Agent#response_follow_meta_refresh when Mechanize#follow_meta_refresh is enabled. A page containing a meta refresh to another origin causes headers configured through Mechanize#request_headers= to be reapplied to the refresh request, allowing an attacker who controls content in the crawl to capture bearer tokens or session cookies. The default configuration is not affected because follow_meta_refresh is false, and the exposure is limited to caller-supplied default headers. This issue is fixed in version 2.14.1.

cna.title: AdonisJS: Unencoded route parameters can produce open redirects

descriptions.value: AdonisJS HTTP Server is a package for handling HTTP requests in the AdonisJS framework. Prior to 8.2.3 and 9.3.0, AdonisJS HTTP Server inserts route parameter values into URLs without encodeURIComponent in the shared createURL() helper used by Router.makeUrl() and Response.redirect().toRoute(). If an application places attacker-controlled data in a dynamic first path segment and uses the generated route URL as a redirect destination, a value beginning with a slash can produce a scheme-relative external URL. Wildcard parameters are affected by the same missing encoding, while APIs intentionally accepting complete redirect URLs are not affected. An attacker can redirect users from a trusted application to an attacker-controlled site, facilitating phishing or abuse of authentication and OAuth flows. This issue is fixed in versions 8.2.3 and 9.3.0.

cna.title: msgpack5: Truncated map32 headers throw an unexpected error

descriptions.value: msgpack5 is a msgpack v5 implementation for node.js and the browser. Prior to 6.1.0, the decoder reads the four-byte length of a map32 value before validating that the complete five-byte header is available. A truncated map32 header therefore causes a checked out-of-bounds buffer read and throws RangeError instead of IncompleteBufferError, which can unexpectedly terminate a request, stream, or worker in applications that wait for additional bytes after IncompleteBufferError. There is no adjacent-memory disclosure because the buffer implementation checks bounds. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.0.

cna.title: Foreman: api filter lookup ignores a search-limited filter permission

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Wenhao Wu (Southeast University) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Filter creation, update, and deletion are audited with the role. Review recent filter audit records for deletions and role changes by delegated filter administrators. Removing those two permissions from delegated roles, or leaving them unlimited and held only by fully trusted administrators, closes the path until a fix is available.

descriptions.value: A flaw has been found in **permission filters** in the **foreman** package. The API loads a filter by its identifier and does not apply the search limit on the caller's permission. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already be allowed to delete filters for one role only. They can delete filters that belong to other unlocked roles. Those other roles then lose the access the deleted filters had granted.

cna.title: Channel tokens and organization API key exposed in API responses

descriptions.value: A third-party OAuth app permitted to delete a channel obtains that channel's social platform access and refresh tokens and can act on the connected account outside Postiz.
An organization member without the admin role obtains the organization API key and can use the public API on behalf of the organization.

timeline.value: Postiz has developed and verified a patch.
Postiz has created the release and published the advisory.

descriptions.value:
Several Postiz endpoints return the complete database row of the record they operate on instead of only the fields the client needs. Two of them include secrets the caller is not meant to receive.

The public API's channel delete returns the deleted integration row, including the channel's platform access token and refresh token. A third-party OAuth app permitted to delete a channel therefore receives that channel's social platform credentials and can use them against the connected account directly, outside Postiz.

`GET /user/organizations` returns each organization row, including its API key, to every member of the organization. The API key is intended for admins only, so a member with a lower role can obtain it and call the public API on behalf of the organization.

Both endpoints require a valid session, API key or OAuth token and are scoped to the caller's own organization. There is no anonymous access and no cross-tenant exposure.

cna.title: MariaDB Connector/Node.js: Uncaught exception crashes the client during ed25519 authentication with zero-configuration TLS

descriptions.value: MariaDB Connector/Node.js is used to connect applications developed on Node.js to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.3.0 until 3.5.4, the zero-configuration TLS fingerprint-validation path calls Ed25519PasswordAuth.hash() through Authentication.validateFingerPrint, but Ed25519PasswordAuth.hash() references a seed identifier that is not in scope. Exposure requires a MariaDB server reached over TCP, TLS enabled with ssl: true or an ssl object whose rejectUnauthorized value is not false, a password set, no ssl.ca configured, and client_ed25519 negotiated as the authentication plugin. Under those conditions, a legitimate server, malicious server, or network attacker presenting a self-signed certificate can reach this path and cause a synchronous ReferenceError to escape the socket data handler. Under Node.js default uncaught-exception behavior, the client process terminates, causing denial of service. Configurations using a provided CA, rejectUnauthorized: false, another authentication plugin, or a Unix socket do not reach this vulnerable path. This issue is fixed in version 3.5.4.

descriptions.value: Pydantic AI is a Python agent framework for building applications and workflows with Generative AI. From 1.56.0 until 1.107.6 and 2.44.0, applications that opt attacker-influenced URLs into local network access through FileUrl with force_download='allow-local' or web_fetch_tool with allow_local_urls=True can bypass the cloud-metadata blocklist by appending an IPv6 zone identifier to an IPv6 metadata address. IPv6Address equality and hashing include the zone identifier, so the blocklist comparison fails even though the network stack ignores the zone on a non-link-local destination and reaches the metadata service, potentially exposing cloud IAM credentials. The opt-in settings are disabled by default, and the issue requires an IPv6-enabled environment. This issue is fixed in versions 1.107.6 and 2.44.0.

The save-time sanitizer mbw_htmlspecialchars2() is ineffective against this vector because the exploit payload relies solely on unquoted HTML attribute syntax using only spaces, alphanumerics, and characters such as =, parentheses, and dots — none of which are escaped.

cna.title: Excelize: RIGHT() on supplementary-plane text slices with a negative index and panics

descriptions.value: Excelize is a Go language library for reading and writing Microsoft Excel spreadsheets. From 2.10.1 to 2.11.0, RIGHT validates the requested length with UTF-16 code-unit counts but slices a rune array using Unicode code-point counts. RIGHT reaches leftRight through CalcCellValue, where countUTF16String validates one unit but utf8.RuneCountInString supplies the slice index in another. When RIGHT evaluates supplementary-plane text with a requested character count between the rune count and UTF-16 code-unit count, the inconsistent units produce a negative rune-slice index, allowing an attacker to panic during formula evaluation. No fixed version is available as of this review.

cna.title: datamodel-code-generator: Protobuf weak-import path traversal allows files to be written outside the temporary directory

descriptions.value: datamodel-code-generator generates Python data models from schema definitions. From 0.59.0 until 0.81.0, an attacker-controlled Protobuf schema can supply absolute or parent-directory paths captured by WEAK_IMPORT_PATTERN and consumed by _write_missing_weak_imports in src/datamodel_code_generator/parser/protobuf.py. Exploitation requires a victim or automated job to process the attacker-controlled schema with Protobuf input support, which requires the grpcio-tools package. The paths escape the weak_imports temporary directory before protoc runs, allowing creation of directory trees and new files or overwrite of existing writable files with a generated Protobuf syntax declaration. The effect persists when later Protobuf compilation fails. The written content is limited to a proto2 or proto3 syntax declaration, and direct arbitrary code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.81.0.

cna.title: Not Failing Securely ('Failing Open') in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which treats an incomplete, unsigned or unproven DNSSEC answer for a TLSA or MX lookup under a signed zone as indeterminate, does not use a mail exchanger whose lookup was indeterminate, defers the delivery when none is left, delivers only to mail exchangers named by a DNSSEC-validated MX record set, and (for a host whose DNS servers are IPv6 only) asks those IPv6 servers. Until then, for each recipient domain whose mail must be protected, an SMTP route that names its mail exchangers with the connection security 'STARTTLS (required)', with remote certificate verification on (VerifyRemoteSslCertificate=1), prevents delivery in cleartext or to another host for that domain; and the server's DNS resolver should be one reached over a trusted path, such as a validating resolver on the same host.

descriptions.value: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 fails open when applying DANE (RFC 7672) to outbound SMTP delivery. The server's validating DNSSEC resolver treated a TLSA or MX lookup that did not complete (no answer, SERVFAIL, a malformed reply), an answer without the requested records and without an NSEC/NSEC3 proof of their absence, and an answer whose records carried no applicable RRSIG as if the recipient domain were unsigned, and from 6.2.19 it also delivered to mail exchangers taken from an unvalidated MX lookup that the DNSSEC-validated MX record set did not name. An attacker who can drop, forge or strip DNS answers on the path to the server's resolver, at the resolver, or between the resolver and the recipient domain's name servers, and who holds an active position on the SMTP path, can thereby disable DANE for a DNSSEC-signed recipient domain and cause messages to be delivered in cleartext or to a host of the attacker's choosing with an arbitrary certificate, where they can be read and modified.

cna.title: MariaDB Connector/Node.js: SQL injection in the text protocol when the session uses NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES

descriptions.value: MariaDB Connector/Node.js is used to connect applications developed on Node.js to MariaDB and MySQL databases. Prior to 3.2.5, 3.3.4, 3.4.7, and 3.5.4, text-protocol escaping always prefixes quotes with a backslash and does not honor the session's NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode, including in Connection.escape(). When that mode is enabled, the backslash is an ordinary character, so an attacker-controlled placeholder value can close the SQL string literal and inject arbitrary SQL with the application's database privileges. The vulnerable configuration may be enabled server-wide, through connector initialization options, or with an application-issued SET sql_mode; execute() and batch() use binary protocols and are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 3.2.5, 3.3.4, 3.4.7, and 3.5.4.

cna.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which reads X-hMailServer-LoopCount in one validated place (a count only when it is digits and never above the limit; anything else is read as the limit so no generated mail is made from it), holds a Sieve notify to the same limit, and refuses an account Sieve script or rule that edits the counter, and writes a line break in a header value as spaces unless it folds the line, so that no value a generated message is built from writes a field of its own. Until then there is no setting that stops the header being read or that turns Sieve off: reduce forwarding and auto-reply arrangements that can feed one another, keep the Sieve script surfaces closed to accounts (ManageSieveServerPort=0, the default, and the REST API off where it is not needed, RestApiPort=0, the default), review active Sieve scripts and account rules for a notify of the account's own address and for an edit of X-hMailServer-LoopCount, and watch the queue for a message generated far past the loop limit.

descriptions.value: Unchecked input for a loop condition in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to stop the server carrying mail. The server bounds the mail it generates in response to a message - a rule forward, reply or copy, an account forward, a Sieve redirect, vacation or notify, a bounce, an out-of-office reply - by a counter it carries in the message's X-hMailServer-LoopCount header, and makes no more once the counter reaches the configured rule loop limit (5 by default); that is what ends a forwarding or auto-reply cycle in a bounded number of hops. X-hMailServer-LoopCount is an ordinary header that is not stripped from mail arriving from outside, and the server read it with a signed conversion and no validation, so a count below zero passed every test against the limit: a sender who sets X-hMailServer-LoopCount to a negative value, or on the Linux builds to a value above the 32-bit signed range that the conversion wraps to a negative one, lifts the bound, and a message that enters a generated-mail cycle then loops up to about two thousand million times, each hop a queued message and a delivery, filling the queue and disk and stopping mail service. The Sieve notify action (from 6.2.22) consulted no limit at all, and its increment of the count could overflow a signed integer; and an account could reset the counter on its own mail through a Sieve editheader of the header (from 6.2.22) or a rule Set header value action (all versions) ahead of a forward or redirect.

cna.title: Contao: Improper access control in the table access voter

descriptions.value: Contao is an Open Source CMS. From version 5.7.0 until 5.7.12, TableAccessVoter::hasAccessToModule() in core-bundle/src/Security/Voter/DataContainer/TableAccessVoter.php caches authorization decisions using only $tokenHash, a hash of the user's security token, and omits the table returned by getDataSource(). If one request first checks a table allowed to the user and then a different denied table, the voter can reuse the allowed result, while DefaultDataContainerVoter can convert an incorrect abstention into a grant. A low-privileged backend user can consequently read, create, update, or delete records in tables outside assigned module permissions, including tables containing member or newsletter-subscriber data. This issue is fixed in version 5.7.12.

cna.title: Nginx-UI AuthRequired token cookie fallback enables CSRF against management APIs

descriptions.value: Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. From 2.0.0 until 2.5.0, AuthRequired accepts a browser-managed token cookie as an API credential after the front end stores the JWT in that cookie. Because management endpoints do not universally require a CSRF token or perform Origin or Referer validation, a remote attacker can induce a logged-in administrator's browser to submit authenticated cross-site state-changing requests, including POST /api/configs. The attack requires an administrator account without OTP/Passkey or a target endpoint that does not require secure-session proof. The attacker cannot read the cross-origin response but can modify Nginx configuration, trigger reloads, or invoke other management operations reachable with the victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.0.

cna.title: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which removes a MIME parameter and deletes header fields in a single pass and searches an encoded word's terminator only for a decodable word. Until then: lower the maximum message size (which bounds the quadratic paths but not the non-terminating one), and restart the service to end a hung thread.

descriptions.value: Inefficient algorithmic complexity and a non-terminating loop in the MIME processing of received messages in Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to make the mail services unavailable by sending a message. Removing a MIME header parameter whose value is empty and directly followed by a semicolon (for example a Content-Disposition with 'filename=a.bat; filename=;') entered a loop that never terminates, holding a worker thread at full load until the server is restarted; this is reached when the attachment blocker renames a blocked attachment or a filename is set over the REST API. Separately, decoding a header field that holds many RFC 2047 encoded words of an encoding other than base64 or quoted-printable, removing a parameter with many RFC 2231 continuations, and deleting many header fields of one name each took time growing with the square of the message, on the small thread pools that serve IMAP, SMTP and POP3 connections, delivery and the REST API.

From 2.7.1 to 2.11.0, mergeCellsParser leaves the cached rectangle empty for an empty mergeCell ref and then passes that empty slice to cellInRange without a length check. GetCellValue reaches mergeCellsParser, which passes an empty rectangle derived from the mergeCell ref attribute into cellInRange. When a crafted worksheet contains an empty mergeCell ref and a non-streaming cell API reads the worksheet, cellInRange indexes four positions in an empty slice, allowing an attacker to panic on the first affected cell operation. cna.title: Apache CXF: The Netty HTTP client transport does not perform TLS hostname verification.

credits.value: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

descriptions.value:
In Apache CXF, the Netty-based HTTP client transport (cxf-rt-transports-http-netty-client) did not verify that the hostname in the server’s TLS certificate matched the host being called. This applied over both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, even when disableCNCheck was left at its default value of false. The certificate chain was validated against the configured trust store, but the endpoint’s identity was not. A network attacker able to intercept traffic could present any certificate trusted by the client, such as a publicly issued certificate for a domain they control, and impersonate the target service. They could then read or modify the exchanged messages, including credentials. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

cna.title: Missing Authorization in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which refuses a Sieve script that adds or deletes From, Sender, Resent-From, Resent-Sender or DKIM-Signature when the script is stored, and does not make such an edit at delivery for a script stored earlier (logged), while leaving Reply-To and other fields editable; and which lets only a server rule's Set header value action, which only the server administrator saves, set those five fields, refusing an account's or a domain's rule that sets one when it is saved and not setting it at delivery for one stored before (logged). Until then, where accounts need not set Sieve scripts, close the script surfaces: keep ManageSieve off (ManageSieveServerPort=0, the default) or bound to the loopback, and turn the REST API off where the webmail's filter editor is not wanted (RestApiPort=0, the default); and review active Sieve scripts for an addheader or deleteheader of From, Sender, Resent-From, Resent-Sender or DKIM-Signature followed by a redirect, and account and domain rules for a Set header value of one of those fields. There is no per-extension setting that turns editheader off while Sieve is in use.

descriptions.value: Missing authorization in the Sieve editheader action (6.2.22 through 6.3.6) and in the mail-rule Set header value action (6.0.0 through 6.3.6) of Progressive Robot hMailServer allows an authenticated user to make the server send mail as any address, DKIM-signed where the address is at a domain the server signs for. A Sieve script's editheader (addheader/deleteheader) could add or delete any header field except Received and Return-Path, and the server applies a script's header edits before it queues a redirect, so the redirected copy is sent as the script left it. The server signs a message's first delivery pass as the domain named in its From header wherever it signs DKIM for that domain and the message carries no signature of it. A script could therefore delete and re-add From - another account's address, or anyone's at a hosted domain - and redirect, so the server sent the message in that name and, for a hosted domain, signed it with that domain's DKIM key, a forgery aligned to pass the domain's DMARC; or, where another sender's domain is one the server signs for, delete the DKIM-Signature that sender's message arrived with, alter a field, and redirect, so the server re-signed the altered message as that sender's domain. editheader placed no restriction on From, Sender, Resent-From, Resent-Sender or DKIM-Signature. The editheader action was introduced in 6.2.22. In the mail-rule engine, a domain's or an account's rule's Set header value action could likewise set From, Sender, Resent-From, Resent-Sender or DKIM-Signature ahead of a forward or a copy, whoever the rule belonged to, so that an account acting on its own rules over COM, a domain administrator, or an API key confined to a domain (over the REST API from 6.3.4) could have the server forward or copy a message in the name of any address, signed, where that address is at a domain the server hosts with DKIM signing enabled, with that domain's key.

descriptions.value: svg-sanitizer is a PHP SVG/XML sanitizer. Prior to 1.0.0, Resolver::processReferences() in src/ElementReference/Resolver.php builds the SVG <use> reference graph with a case-sensitive href attribute predicate before cleanHrefAttributes() normalizes mixed-case names. An attacker can provide xlink:HrEf on nested <use> elements so the graph omits those references, after which the sanitizer converts the attribute to canonical xlink:href and returns the live nesting structure without applying the useNestingLimit protection. A consuming application that renders the sanitized SVG can therefore be exposed to the resource exhaustion that control is designed to prevent. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.0.

cna.title: Foreman: domain and subnet interface api skips host search filters

workarounds.value: Red Hat is not aware of a practical temporary workaround that fully mitigates this issue or meets Red Hat Product Security's standards for usability, deployment, applicability, or stability. Customers are advised to apply the relevant security updates when they become available.

descriptions.value: An **incorrect authorization** flaw has been found in **network interface handling** in the **Foreman** package. The domain and subnet interface API checks only that the caller holds a host permission. It does not apply the search limit on that permission, so the request is answered from every interface on the domain or subnet. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already be allowed to view some hosts and to view a domain or subnet shared with other hosts. They can request that domain or subnet's interfaces. The response includes interface records of hosts they are not allowed to view. If the attacker or user is also allowed to edit some hosts, they can submit a change to one of those interfaces. The interface is then saved with that change.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [login] Let only one request spend an e-mailed OTP

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [login] Let only one request spend an e-mailed OTP
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix makes OTP consumption atomic by moving the deletion of the OTP from the shared store into the validation condition itself. The return value of the delete operation (1 if the key was actually removed, 0 otherwise) is now part of the success check, so only the request that successfully removes the OTP from the store is permitted to proceed with login. A session-state cleanup call was also added to remove the OTP user reference from the session.
assumptions: The exact affected version range is not explicitly stated in the patch; the tag boundary v2.5.48 with 39 commits after the fix suggests the fix landed shortly after that tag, but the precise first-fixed version is unconfirmed.
The CAPEC-111 mapping is the closest available; no CAPEC specifically covers OTP replay via race condition, so this is the best-fit pattern.
CVSS AC:H assumes the race window is narrow and requires precise timing; if the Redis round-trip latency is large, exploitation may be easier, but no evidence supports lowering AC.
The commit message states the issue was 'found during the internal review, not externally reported,' but no specific individual is named as finder, so no finder credit is assigned.
PR:N assumes the attacker obtains the OTP through out-of-band means (email interception); if MISP requires prior authentication to request an OTP, PR could be L.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In UsersController::email_otp(), the $redis->del() call was moved from after the hash_equals comparison into the if-condition as an additional conjunct. The condition now requires $redis->del('misp:otp:' . $user_id) === 1, meaning only the request whose delete actually removed the key (returning 1) can proceed to Auth->login(). A $this->Session->delete('email_otp_user') call was added before the login step to clean up session state. Net change: 6 insertions, 3 deletions in one file.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: Exploitation occurs over the network via HTTP POST. AC:H: Exploiting the race condition requires precise timing of two concurrent requests so both read the OTP before either deletes it; this is non-trivial to achieve reliably. AT:N: No data corruption or manipulation is required. PR:N: The attacker does not need prior authentication to MISP; they only need possession of a valid OTP (e.g., intercepted email). UI:N: No victim interaction beyond the initial login flow is needed. VC:N: No direct confidentiality loss of system data. VI:L: The one-time-use property of the OTP is violated, allowing a second authenticated session. VA:N: No availability impact. SC/SI:L: Limited integrity impact on the authentication process; no cross-system impact. SA:N: No impact on security authority.

capecRationale.rationale: The attack pattern involves an adversary issuing two or more concurrent requests to exploit a non-atomic check-and-use sequence on a shared resource (the OTP in Redis). CAPEC-111 directly describes exploiting timing dependencies between sub-processes. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed vulnerability; no more specific CAPEC for OTP replay via race condition exists in the CAPEC catalog.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The OTP stored in Redis is a shared resource accessed by concurrent HTTP requests. The original code performed read, compare, and delete as separate non-atomic operations, allowing two concurrent requests to both read and validate the same OTP before either deletes it. This is a textbook race condition on a shared resource.

The check (reading and comparing the OTP) and the use (logging in) are separated in time, and the state (OTP presence in the store) can change between the two steps due to a concurrent request. This is a TOCTOU variant of the race condition.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a race condition in the email-based one-time password (OTP) login flow. When two HTTP requests carrying the same valid OTP are submitted concurrently, both can successfully authenticate and establish a session. The root cause is that the OTP value is read from the shared store, validated, and then deleted in separate non-atomic steps, allowing a second in-flight request to read the same value before the first request's deletion takes effect.

Preconditions:

- The target MISP instance has email OTP login enabled.

- The attacker possesses a valid, unexpired OTP (e.g., via email interception or social engineering).

- The attacker can issue two HTTP POST requests in close temporal proximity.

Impact:

- The one-time-use guarantee of the OTP is violated; a single code can yield two authenticated sessions.

- This weakens the authentication control and may facilitate unauthorized access if the OTP is shared or intercepted.

Affected versions: <2.5.48

patches.subject: fix: [login] enforce TOTP enrolment on AJAX requests
fix: [login] Refuse every unenrolled session request, not

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [login] Refuse every unenrolled session request, not
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The TOTP enrolment enforcement in the user verification path was extended from covering only standard browser requests to covering all non-browser request types (AJAX, REST, .json, automation). Any request that cannot follow the browser redirect to the TOTP setup page is now refused with a 403 Forbidden response if the user has not enrolled in TOTP and the instance requires it. Identities authenticated via API key remain exempt, as they are not browser sessions subject to the redirect-based enrolment flow.
assumptions: The affected MISP version range is not specified in the patch metadata; the vulnerability is assumed to affect all versions prior to the fix commits (8deb0619e and 6b527ba6e) that contain the otp_required enforcement logic without the non-browser request guard.

The CAPEC-128 mapping is approximate; the bypass is of an authentication requirement (forced TOTP enrolment) rather than a traditional authorization rule, but CAPEC-128 is the closest available pattern for exploiting an access control that is not uniformly applied across all request paths.

CVSS VC:H assumes that bypassing the mandatory 2FA requirement constitutes a high confidentiality impact on the vulnerability component, as the instance-level security policy (requiring all users to have 2FA) is nullified for the affected user. If the instance's threat model considers 2FA as a defense-in-depth layer rather than a primary control, VC could be rated Lower.

The patch evidence does not indicate whether the vulnerability is exploitable by an external unauthenticated attacker; the analysis assumes the attacker is an authenticated user (PR:L) who has not yet enrolled in TOTP.
The two commits are treated as a single vulnerability per the patch_set_assumption; the first commit is an incomplete fix and the second is the complete fix.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Controller/AppController.php, the __verifyUser method was modified. Patch 1 added a conditional block after the $isUserRequest definition that checks: the request is not a standard user request, it is an AJAX request, the user has no TOTP configured, Security.otp_required is enabled, the role does not have perm_skip_otp, and the current action is not one of the allowed exceptions (terms, change_pw, logout, login, totp_new). If all conditions are met, a ForbiddenException is thrown. Patch 2 replaced the $this->request->is('ajax') condition with empty($user['logged_by_authkey']), broadening the guard to all non-browser request types while explicitly exempting API-key-authenticated sessions.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N - the bypass is achieved over the network via HTTP requests. AC:L - the attack is trivially simple: change the request type (add X-Requested-With header, append .json, use REST endpoint). AT:N - no special target conditions. PR:L - the attacker needs a valid authenticated session (low privilege: any user account). UI:N - no victim interaction beyond the attacker's own request. VC:H - the two-factor authentication requirement is completely bypassed, meaning the confidentiality protection provided by mandatory 2FA is nullified; the user retains full data access without the second factor. VI:N, VA:N - no integrity or availability impact on the MISP component. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N - no impact on subsequent components. The primary impact is the bypass of an authentication control (confidentiality of the 2FA gate).

capecRationale.rationale: The access control policy requiring TOTP enrolment is incorrectly scoped to only standard browser requests. An attacker (or the legitimate user) exploits this misconfiguration by issuing requests in a non-browser format (AJAX, REST, .json) that the access control check does not cover. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed bypass of a security control due to incomplete scoping of the enforcement logic. The mapping is approximate because the bypass is of an authentication requirement rather than a traditional authorization rule, but CAPEC-128 best captures the pattern of exploiting an access control that is not uniformly applied.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The TOTP (two-factor) authentication requirement is not properly enforced across all request types. The authentication gate (forced TOTP enrolment) is bypassed for non-browser requests, allowing a user to operate without completing the required second factor. This is a failure to properly enforce an authentication requirement.

The critical function of enforcing TOTP enrolment on otp_required instances is missing for AJAX, REST, .json, and automation request paths. The authentication check is present for browser requests but absent for all other request shapes, constituting a missing authentication control on a critical security function.

descriptions.value:
On MISP instances configured to require TOTP enrolment (Security.otp_required), the enforcement of the mandatory two-factor authentication setup applied only to standard browser requests. An authenticated user who had not yet enrolled in TOTP could bypass the forced setup by issuing any non-browser request type, including AJAX/XHR calls, REST API requests, .json format URLs, restSearch queries, or automation actions. Because these machine-readable request shapes cannot follow the redirect that the browser path uses to send the user to the TOTP enrolment page, the guard simply skipped the check and the user retained full access to the instance without completing the required second-factor setup.

The initial fix (commit 8deb0619e) added a guard specifically for AJAX requests. A follow-up fix (commit 6b527ba6e) broadened the guard to cover every non-browser request shape, while preserving the exemption for identities authenticated via API key (logged_by_authkey flag).

Impact: an authenticated user on an otp_required instance can operate with full access indefinitely without enrolling in TOTP, nullifying the instance-level two-factor authentication policy.

Affected version: <2.5.48

supportingMedia.value:
XML injection in the encoder of Saxy. Saxy.Encoder does not neutralize the -- sequence in XML comment content: escape_comment/2 returns the comment binary unchanged in every clause and only appends a space when the comment ends in a single -, so neither an interior -- nor a full --> is escaped or rejected before the encoder wraps the content in the <!-- and --> delimiters.

When an application serializes attacker-controlled text as a comment, through Saxy.XML.comment/1 or a raw {:comment, text} simple form child, the attacker can close the comment early with --> and inject arbitrary sibling markup into the serialized document. A downstream parser then sees elements, attributes, and text that the application never built. Where the document is rendered as HTML or SVG, the injected markup executes as stored cross-site scripting; where it is consumed by another XML processor, the attacker can forge data that the producing application never emitted. Documents that Saxy only parses are not a vector.

This issue affects saxy: from 0.7.0 before 1.7.0.

cna.title: Livebook Teams identity callback lacks state binding, allowing login CSRF

descriptions.value: CAPEC-62 Cross Site Request Forgery

references.name: Livebook Teams Identity OAuth-style callback has no state/nonce binding, enabling login CSRF

descriptions.value:
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in livebook-dev livebook allows an attacker to authenticate a victim's browser session under the attacker's own Livebook Teams identity.

When Livebook is configured to use Livebook Teams for identity, Livebook.ZTA.LivebookTeams.handle_request/4 in lib/livebook/zta/livebook_teams.ex handles the OAuth-style callback carrying a teams_identity marker and a code parameter. The clause exchanges that code for an access token and writes the token into the browser session without verifying any value that ties the callback to the browser session that started the login. No state or nonce is generated when the flow is initiated: Livebook.Teams.Requests.create_auth_request/1 in lib/livebook/teams/requests.ex sends an empty request body, so no per-attempt value is ever registered, and the callback clause has nothing to compare against.

An attacker who holds membership in the same Livebook Teams organisation as the target instance can therefore begin the login flow themselves, retain the resulting authorization code without redeeming it, and induce a victim to open a crafted URL carrying that code. The victim's browser completes the exchange and the resulting session is bound to the attacker's identity rather than the victim's. The victim is not required to hold any particular privilege, and no credential belonging to the victim is involved. The vulnerability does not allow the attacker to authenticate as the victim.

The consequence is that a user believes they are working in their own authenticated session while they are in fact operating as another identity. Work performed in that session is attributed to the attacker's account, and secrets, uploaded data, or notebook results the victim produces are exposed to the attacker rather than kept in the victim's own account. The authorization code must be redeemed within a short window after the login flow begins, which constrains the timing of the attack but not its feasibility.

This issue affects livebook: from 0.15.0 before 0.18.7 and from 0.19.0 before 0.19.9.

cna.title: RabbitMQ: Stored XSS via TLS peer-certificate DN in management UI

descriptions.value: RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. Prior to versions 3.13.15, 4.0.20, 4.1.11, and 4.2.6, The management UI uses EJS 1.0 in which <%= ... %> does NOT HTML-escape. connection.ejs:135 renders <%= connection.ssl_details.peer_cert_subject %> (and peer_cert_issuer) directly into the page. The same pattern appears in streamConnection.ejs:102,106,110. The values come from rabbit_ssl:peer_cert_subject/1 which formats the DN as a string without HTML escaping. The verifier corrected the original researcher's claim: this is reachable only when the listener is configured with verify_peer (so the certificate must be signed by a CA in the broker's trust store, not arbitrary self-signed); however, in deployments using mTLS for client authentication, any user who can request a certificate from the organisational CA controls the Subject CN. An attacker who can obtain a TLS client certificate signed by a CA the broker trusts (with verify_peer enabled) can embed JavaScript in the certificate's Subject DN. When any administrator views that connection in the management UI, the script executes in the admin's browser session, allowing full account takeover (create users, export definitions, etc.). The management UI's CSP includes 'unsafe-inline', so inline script execution is not blocked. Preconditions include TLS listener configured with ssl_options.verify = verify_peer Attacker can obtain a CA-signed client certificate with attacker-chosen Subject (e.g. self-service corporate PKI, or rabbitmq_trust_store plugin in use) Administrator views the connection detail page. This issue is fixed in versions 3.13.15, 4.0.20, 4.1.11, and 4.2.6.

cna.title: Path traversal in imported file_entries name allows arbitrary file write via URL-type entry download

descriptions.value: CAPEC-76 Manipulating Web Input to File System Calls

references.name: Path traversal via unsanitized file_entries name on notebook import (arbitrary local file write)

descriptions.value:
Relative Path Traversal vulnerability in livebook-dev livebook allows an attacker-authored notebook to write a file with attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary path.

A .livemd notebook can declare file_entries metadata, each entry carrying a name. Every path that creates a file entry through the user interface validates that name with Livebook.Notebook.validate_file_entry_name/2, which requires a flat filename of alphanumerics, dashes, underscores and dots, ending in an extension. The import path does not: Livebook.LiveMarkdown.Import.file_entry_metadata_to_attrs/1 in lib/livebook/live_markdown/import.ex takes the name verbatim from the notebook source.

For a URL-type file entry, Livebook.Session.file_entry_cache_file/2 in lib/livebook/session.ex resolves that name beneath the session's temporary directory without checking that the result stays inside it, and Livebook.FileSystem.Utils.resolve_unix_like_path/2 collapses parent-directory segments while clamping only at the filesystem root. When the entry's content is requested and no cached copy exists, Livebook fetches the entry's URL and writes the response body to the resolved path, creating parent directories as needed. The attacker therefore controls both the destination and the contents of the written file, which may land anywhere the Livebook process can write. The same missing containment check is present in Livebook.Session.to_attachment_file_entry/2.

A victim who opens an attacker-supplied notebook and causes the entry to be fetched triggers the write within their own authenticated session; the attacker needs no account on the target instance. URL-type entries are also not placed under notebook stamping quarantine on import, so no warning is shown.

This issue affects livebook: from 0.11.0 before 0.18.7 and from 0.19.0 before 0.19.9.
